from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Pt, Inches
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.enum.text import MSO_AUTO_SIZE

# ---------------- Design system (topic: sky / aerial networks) ----------------
DARK    = RGBColor(0x0B, 0x1F, 0x3A)   # deep navy (title / conclusion)
PRIMARY = RGBColor(0x12, 0x4E, 0x89)   # sky blue (headings)
TEAL    = RGBColor(0x2A, 0x9D, 0x8F)   # accent for quotes
ACCENT  = RGBColor(0xE8, 0x8A, 0x2B)   # warm accent (dark-slide headings)
CARD    = RGBColor(0xEE, 0xF2, 0xF7)   # light card fill
DCARD   = RGBColor(0x16, 0x30, 0x55)   # dark card fill
LINE    = RGBColor(0xD5, 0xDD, 0xE5)   # card border
WHITE   = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
TEXT    = RGBColor(0x20, 0x24, 0x28)
MUTED   = RGBColor(0x5A, 0x63, 0x70)

prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width  = Inches(13.333)
prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)
BLANK = prs.slide_layouts[6]

def bg(slide, color):
    f = slide.background.fill
    f.solid(); f.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_text(slide, x, y, w, h):
    tb = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(x), Inches(y), Inches(w), Inches(h))
    tb.text_frame.word_wrap = True
    return tb, tb.text_frame

# item tuple: (text, level, bold, color, size, italic)
def H(t, color=PRIMARY, size=17): return (t, 0, True, color, size, False)
def B(t, color=TEXT, size=13):     return ("\u2022  " + t, 1, False, color, size, False)
def Q(t, size=12.5):               return ("\u201c" + t + "\u201d", 1, False, TEAL, size, True)
def HD(t):                         return (t, 0, True, ACCENT, 17, False)
def BD(t):                         return ("\u2022  " + t, 1, False, WHITE, 13, False)
def QD(t):                         return ("\u201c" + t + "\u201d", 1, False, TEAL, 12.5, True)

def render(tf, items):
    tf.clear()
    first = True
    for spec in items:
        text, lvl, bold, color, size, ital = spec
        p = tf.paragraphs[0] if first else tf.add_paragraph()
        first = False
        p.text = text
        p.level = lvl
        p.space_after = Pt(4)
        p.space_before = Pt(0)
        for r in p.runs:
            r.font.size = Pt(size)
            r.font.bold = bold
            r.font.italic = ital
            r.font.name = "Arial"
            r.font.color.rgb = color

def card(slide, x, y, w, h, items, dark=False):
    sp = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE,
                                Inches(x), Inches(y), Inches(w), Inches(h))
    sp.fill.solid()
    sp.fill.fore_color.rgb = DCARD if dark else CARD
    sp.line.color.rgb = LINE
    sp.line.width = Pt(0.75)
    sp.shadow.inherit = False
    tf = sp.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    tf.margin_left = Inches(0.18); tf.margin_right = Inches(0.18)
    tf.margin_top = Inches(0.14);  tf.margin_bottom = Inches(0.14)
    render(tf, items)
    tf.auto_size = MSO_AUTO_SIZE.TEXT_TO_FIT_SHAPE   # shrink-to-fit, never overflow
    return sp

def content_slide(title, columns, dark=False):
    s = prs.slides.add_slide(BLANK)
    bg(s, DARK if dark else WHITE)
    tb, tf = add_text(s, 0.6, 0.32, 12.1, 1.0)
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]; p.text = title
    p.font.size = Pt(27); p.font.bold = True
    p.font.name = "Arial"; p.font.color.rgb = (WHITE if dark else PRIMARY)
    n = len(columns)
    if n == 1:
        card(s, 0.6, 1.5, 12.1, 5.4, columns[0], dark=dark)
    else:
        cw = 5.9
        for i, col in enumerate(columns):
            card(s, 0.6 + i * 6.23, 1.5, cw, 5.4, col, dark=dark)
    return s

# ---------------- Slide 1: Title (dark) ----------------
s = prs.slides.add_slide(BLANK)
bg(s, DARK)
tb, tf = add_text(s, 0.8, 1.9, 11.7, 2.4)
p = tf.paragraphs[0]; p.text = "A Survey on Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) Communications"
p.font.size = Pt(34); p.font.bold = True; p.font.name = "Arial"; p.font.color.rgb = WHITE
p2 = tf.add_paragraph(); p2.text = "State-of-the-Art, Existing Standards, and Future Directions"
p2.font.size = Pt(20); p2.font.color.rgb = TEAL; p2.font.name = "Arial"; p2.space_before = Pt(8)
tb2, tf2 = add_text(s, 0.8, 6.4, 11.7, 0.8)
p3 = tf2.paragraphs[0]; p3.text = "Full-paper reading & content summary   \u2022   Week 1   \u2022   ML in Wireless Networks"
p3.font.size = Pt(13); p3.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0xB8, 0xC4, 0xD4); p3.font.name = "Arial"

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Pt, Inches
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.enum.text import MSO_AUTO_SIZE, PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR

# ---------------- Design tokens (60-30-10, aerial/sky theme) ----------------
NAVY     = RGBColor(0x0E, 0x1B, 0x2A)   # dominant dark
PAPER    = RGBColor(0xF4, 0xF6, 0xF8)   # light bg
WHITE    = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
BLUE     = RGBColor(0x2E, 0x6F, 0x9E)   # secondary
AMBER    = RGBColor(0xF2, 0xA9, 0x00)   # accent (sparse)
INK      = RGBColor(0x1B, 0x26, 0x32)   # body text on light
MUTED    = RGBColor(0x5A, 0x66, 0x72)
CARDFILL = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
CARDLINE = RGBColor(0xD9, 0xE0, 0xE6)
QUOTEFILL= RGBColor(0xEA, 0xF1, 0xF7)
DARKCARD = RGBColor(0x16, 0x2B, 0x42)
TITLE_FONT = "Cambria"
BODY_FONT  = "Calibri"

prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width  = Inches(13.333)
prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)
BLANK = prs.slide_layouts[6]

def bg(slide, color):
    f = slide.background.fill; f.solid(); f.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_text(slide, x, y, w, h):
    tb = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(x), Inches(y), Inches(w), Inches(h))
    tb.text_frame.word_wrap = True
    return tb, tb.text_frame

# item tuple: (text, lvl, bold, color, size, italic)
def H(t, color=BLUE, size=15):   return (t, 0, True, color, size, False)
def B(t, color=INK, size=12.5):  return ("\u2022  " + t, 1, False, color, size, False)
def Q(t, size=12):               return ("\u201c" + t + "\u201d", 1, False, BLUE, size, True)
def HD(t):                       return (t, 0, True, AMBER, 15, False)
def BD(t):                       return ("\u2022  " + t, 1, False, WHITE, 12.5, False)
def QD(t):                       return ("\u201c" + t + "\u201d", 1, False, BLUE, 12, True)

def render(tf, items):
    tf.clear(); first = True
    for spec in items:
        text, lvl, bold, color, size, ital = spec
        p = tf.paragraphs[0] if first else tf.add_paragraph()
        first = False
        p.text = text; p.level = lvl
        p.space_after = Pt(3); p.space_before = Pt(0)
        for r in p.runs:
            r.font.size = Pt(size); r.font.bold = bold; r.font.italic = ital
            r.font.name = BODY_FONT; r.font.color.rgb = color

def card(slide, x, y, w, h, items, fill=None, line=None, dark=False, autofit=True):
    if fill is None: fill = DARKCARD if dark else CARDFILL
    if line is None: line = (RGBColor(0x3A, 0x55, 0x72) if dark else CARDLINE)
    sp = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE,
                                Inches(x), Inches(y), Inches(w), Inches(h))
    sp.fill.solid(); sp.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill
    sp.line.color.rgb = line; sp.line.width = Pt(0.75)
    sp.shadow.inherit = False
    tf = sp.text_frame; tf.word_wrap = True
    tf.margin_left = Inches(0.16); tf.margin_right = Inches(0.16)
    tf.margin_top = Inches(0.12);  tf.margin_bottom = Inches(0.12)
    render(tf, items)
    if autofit: tf.auto_size = MSO_AUTO_SIZE.TEXT_TO_FIT_SHAPE
    return sp

def icon_circle(slide, x, y, d, letter, fill=BLUE, txt=WHITE, fs=16):
    c = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, Inches(x), Inches(y), Inches(d), Inches(d))
    c.fill.solid(); c.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill
    c.line.fill.background(); c.shadow.inherit = False
    tf = c.text_frame; tf.word_wrap = False
    tf.margin_top = Inches(0); tf.margin_bottom = Inches(0)
    tf.vertical_anchor = MSO_ANCHOR.MIDDLE
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]; p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER; p.text = letter
    p.font.size = Pt(fs); p.font.bold = True; p.font.name = BODY_FONT; p.font.color.rgb = txt
    return c

def title_band(slide, icon, title, dark=False):
    icon_circle(slide, 0.55, 0.40, 0.64, icon,
                fill=(AMBER if not dark else BLUE), fs=18)
    tb, tf = add_text(slide, 1.38, 0.34, 11.4, 0.9)
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]; p.text = title
    p.font.size = Pt(24); p.font.bold = True; p.font.name = TITLE_FONT
    p.font.color.rgb = (WHITE if dark else BLUE)

def std_slide(icon, title, left, right, dark=False):
    s = prs.slides.add_slide(BLANK); bg(s, NAVY if dark else PAPER)
    title_band(s, icon, title, dark)
    card(s, 0.60, 1.50, 5.90, 5.40, left, dark=dark)
    card(s, 6.83, 1.50, 5.90, 5.40, right, dark=dark)
    return s

def single_slide(icon, title, items, dark=False):
    s = prs.slides.add_slide(BLANK); bg(s, NAVY if dark else PAPER)
    title_band(s, icon, title, dark)
    card(s, 0.60, 1.50, 12.13, 5.40, items, dark=dark)
    return s

PATH: PPT_content/clean_ppt.py

import zipfile, re, shutil, os
from xml.etree import ElementTree as ET

path = r"C:\Users\gbust\Downloads\Academic\Courses\Machine_learning_in_wireless_network\Project1\PPT_content\PPT.pptx"
tmp = path + ".clean.zip"

z = zipfile.ZipFile(path, 'r')
names = z.namelist()
# find duplicate base names
from collections import Counter
base = Counter(n for n in names)
dups = [k for k,c in base.items() if c>1]
print("DUPLICATE ENTRIES:", dups[:20], "..." if len(dups)>20 else "")

# Parse presentation.xml to find referenced slide partnames
pres = z.read('ppt/presentation.xml').decode('utf-8')
rels = z.read('ppt/_rels/presentation.xml.rels').decode('utf-8')
rel_root = ET.fromstring(rels.encode('utf-8'))
ns = {'pr':'http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/relationships'}
# map rId -> Target
rid_target = {}
for rel in rel_root.findall('pr:Relationship', ns):
    rid_target[rel.get('Id')] = rel.get('Target')
# sldId r:ids
sldIds = re.findall(r'<p:sldId[^>]*r:id="(rId\d+)"', pres)
referenced = set()
for rid in sldIds:
    t = rid_target.get(rid)
    if t:
        # Target like 'slides/slide21.xml' relative to ppt/
        referenced.add('ppt/' + t.lstrip('./'))
print("Referenced slide parts:", sorted(referenced))
print("Total slide entries in zip:", [n for n in names if re.match(r'ppt/slides/slide\d+\.xml$', n)])

# Build set of parts to KEEP
# Unreferenced slide parts + their rels are orphans to drop
slide_re = re.compile(r'ppt/slides/slide(\d+)\.xml$')
orphan_slides = set()
for n in names:
    m = slide_re.match(n)
    if m and n not in referenced:
        orphan_slides.add(n)
print("Orphan slide parts to remove:", sorted(orphan_slides))

# Write cleaned zip
keep = []
for n in names:
    if n in orphan_slides:
        continue
    if re.match(r'ppt/slides/_rels/slide\d+\.xml\.rels$', n):
        # keep only if corresponding slide kept
        m = re.search(r'slide(\d+)\.xml\.rels$', n)
        if m and f'ppt/slides/slide{m.group(1)}.xml' not in referenced:
            continue
    keep.append(n)

with zipfile.ZipFile(tmp, 'w', zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as out:
    for n in keep:
        out.writestr(n, z.read(n))
z.close()
shutil.move(tmp, path)
print("Cleaned file written. Kept entries:", len(keep))


================================================================================
PATH: PPT_content/extract_ppt_text.py

from pptx import Presentation

prs = Presentation(r"PPT.pptx")

out_path = r"PPT_content_extracted.txt"

lines = []
lines.append("=" * 60)
lines.append("PPT.pptx Extracted Text (word-for-word)")
lines.append("=" * 60)

for i, slide in enumerate(prs.slides, 1):
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(f"--- Slide {i} ---")
    for shape in slide.shapes:
        if not shape.has_text_frame:
            continue
        for para in shape.text_frame.paragraphs:
            text = para.text.strip()
            if text:
                lines.append(text)

with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write("\n".join(lines))

print(f"Wrote {out_path}")

\documentclass[aspectratio=169,12pt]{beamer}

% ============================================================

% ============================================================
\usetheme{Madrid}
\usecolortheme{whale}
\setbeamertemplate{navigation symbols}{}
\setbeamertemplate{footline}[frame number]

\setbeamersize{
    text margin left=0.5cm,
    text margin right=0.5cm
}
\setbeamertemplate{frametitle}{%
  \nointerlineskip%
  \begin{beamercolorbox}[wd=\paperwidth,ht=2.8ex,dp=1.2ex,leftskip=0.5cm,rightskip=0.5cm]{frametitle}%
    \insertframetitle
  \end{beamercolorbox}%
}

\setlength{\leftmargini}{1.2em}

\setlength{\parskip}{0.3em}

% ============================================================
\title[Fault-Tolerant UAV Networks]
{Persistent, Fault-Tolerant UAV-Based IoT Networks}
\subtitle{MARL-Based Swarm Reconfiguration}
\author{Team -- Intelligent UAV Deployment}
\institute{IIT Dharwad}
\date{}

\begin{document}

% ============================================================
% SLIDE 1 — Title
% ============================================================
\begin{frame}
    \titlepage
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% SLIDE 2 — Problem at a glance
% ============================================================
\begin{frame}{Problem at a Glance}
\begin{center}
\large
$N$ \textbf{drones} fly over $M$ \textbf{ground sensors}.\\[0.4em]
Each drone has a \textbf{finite battery} and can \textbf{fail}.\\[0.4em]
Every sensor needs \textbf{at least $K$ drones} above it \textbf{at all times}.
\end{center}

\vspace{0.6em}
\textbf{Challenge:} coordinate the swarm with \emph{no central controller}.\\
\textbf{Solution:} each drone learns its own policy via multi-agent RL.
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% SLIDE 3 — MDP Formulation
% ============================================================
\begin{frame}{MDP Formulation}
We model the system as a cooperative Dec-POMDP:
\[
\mathcal{G} = \bigl\langle\,
  \underbrace{N}_{\text{agents}},\;
  \underbrace{\mathcal{S}}_{\text{state}},\;
  \underbrace{\{\mathcal{A}_i\}}_{\text{actions}},\;
  \underbrace{\{\mathcal{O}_i\}}_{\text{obs.}},\;
  \underbrace{\mathcal{T}}_{\text{dynamics}},\;
  \underbrace{R}_{\text{reward}},\;
  \underbrace{\gamma}_{\text{discount}}
\,\bigr\rangle
\]

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Objective:} find a policy $\pi$ maximising expected return:
\[
\max_{\pi}\;
\mathbb{E}_{\pi}
\!\left[
  \sum_{t=0}^{T} \gamma^{t}\, R_t
\right]
\]

\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{tabular}{@{}ll@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Symbol} & \textbf{Meaning} \\
\midrule
$N$ & number of active UAV agents \\
$\mathcal{S}$ & global system state space \\
$\mathcal{A}_i$ & action space per UAV \\
$\mathcal{O}_i$ & local observation per UAV \\
$\mathcal{T}$ & state transition dynamics \\
$R$ & cooperative reward function \\
$\gamma \in [0,1)$ & discount factor \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% SLIDE 4 — Global State
% ============================================================
\begin{frame}{Global State $s_t$}
The full system snapshot at time $t$:
\[
s_t = \Bigl\{
  (p_i,\; v_i,\; b_i,\; m_i)_{i=1}^{N},\;\;
  (q_d)_{d=1}^{M},\;\;
  Q_t,\;\;
  F_t
\Bigr\}
\]

\vspace{0.4em}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lll@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Symbol} & \textbf{Meaning} & \textbf{Range} \\
\midrule
$p_i$ & position of UAV $i$ & $\mathbb{R}^3$ \\
$v_i$ & velocity of UAV $i$ & $\|v_i\| \le v_{\max}$ \\
$b_i$ & normalised battery level & $[0,1]$ \\
$m_i$ & operating mode & \{serve, transit, charge\} \\
$q_d$ & position of sensor $d$ & fixed \\
$Q_t$ & charging pad occupancy & $\{0,1\}^S$ \\
$F_t$ & which UAVs have failed & $\{0,1\}^N$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{block}{Key}
The \textbf{centralised critic} sees all of $s_t$ during \textbf{training}.
Each UAV only sees its \textbf{local observation} during \textbf{execution}.
\end{block}
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% SLIDE 5 — Local Observation
% ============================================================
\begin{frame}{Local Observation $o_i$}
Each UAV sees only what is nearby:
\[
o_i = \bigl[
  \underbrace{p_i,\; v_i,\; b_i}_{\text{own state}},\;\;
  \underbrace{\mathcal{N}_i}_{\text{neighbours}},\;\;
  \underbrace{C_i^{\text{local}}}_{\text{local coverage}},\;\;
  \underbrace{\text{risk}_i}_{\text{cut-vertex?}},\;\;
  \underbrace{t_i^{\text{empty}}}_{\text{time-to-empty}},\;\;
  \underbrace{E_i^{\text{station}}}_{\text{energy to pad}}
\bigr]
\]

\vspace{0.4em}
\begin{tabular}{@{}ll@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Symbol} & \textbf{Meaning} \\
\midrule
$\mathcal{N}_i$ & indices of UAVs within $R_{\text{comm}}$ \\
$C_i^{\text{local}}$ & number of local sensors covered \\
$\text{risk}_i$ & $=1$ if removing $i$ disconnects $G_t$ \\
$t_i^{\text{empty}}$ & seconds until battery $\le$ return threshold \\
$E_i^{\text{station}}$ & energy needed to reach nearest pad \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{alertblock}{Decentralised execution}
At deployment: $a_i \sim \pi_\theta(a_i \mid o_i)$ --- no global state needed.
\end{alertblock}
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% SLIDE 6 — Why Decentralised?
% ============================================================
\begin{frame}{Why Not a Central Controller?}
\textbf{Centralised} action space grows exponentially:
\[
|\mathcal{A}| = A^N
\]

\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}ccccc@{}}
\toprule
$N$ & 4 & 6 & 10 & 20 \\
\midrule
$|\mathcal{A}|$ & $5^4 = 625$ & $5^6 = 15625$ & $\sim\!10^7$ & $\sim\!10^{14}$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\vspace{0.4em}
\textbf{Solution:} factorised policy --- each UAV acts independently:
\[
a_i \sim \pi_\theta(a_i \mid o_i)
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
|\mathcal{A}|_{\text{eff}} = A \;\text{ per agent}
\]

\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{block}{Trade-off}
Decentralised is tractable, but each UAV must infer coordination from its local observation $o_i$ alone.
\end{block}
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% SLIDE 7 — Action Space
% ============================================================
\begin{frame}{Action Space $\mathcal{A}_i$}
Each UAV picks one action per time step:
\[
\mathcal{A}_i = \bigl\{
  \text{Hover},\;
  {+x},\; {-x},\; {+y},\; {-y},\;
  \text{Charge}
\bigr\}, \quad |\mathcal{A}_i| = 6
\]

\vspace{0.5em}
\textbf{Movement:}
\[
p_i(t+1) = p_i(t) + v_i(t)\,\Delta t,
\quad \|v_i\| \le v_{\max},\;\; p_i \in \Omega
\]

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Charge is valid only when:}
\[
\|p_i - p_s^{\text{pad}}\| \le d_{\text{charge}}
\quad\text{and}\quad
Q_t[s] = 1 \;\text{(pad is free)}
\]
Otherwise the action defaults to \emph{Hover}.
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% SLIDE 8 — K-Coverage
% ============================================================
\begin{frame}{K-Coverage Requirement}
\textbf{Rule:} every sensor $d$ must have $\ge K$ drones above it.

\vspace{0.4em}
\textbf{Binary coverage} (is UAV $i$ covering sensor $d$?):
\[
x_{id}(t) = \mathbf{1}\!\bigl[\,\|p_i(t) - q_d\| \le R_{\text{cov}}\,\bigr]
\]

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Count per sensor:}
\[
n_d(t) = \sum_{i=1}^{N} x_{id}(t)
\]

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Coverage score:}
\[
C(t) = \frac{1}{M}\sum_{d=1}^{M} \min\!\left(\frac{n_d(t)}{K},\; 1\right)
\]

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Under-coverage rate} (to minimise):
\[
U(t) = \frac{1}{M}\sum_{d=1}^{M} \mathbf{1}\!\bigl[\,n_d(t) < K\,\bigr]
\]
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% SLIDE 9 — Connectivity
% ============================================================
\begin{frame}{Connectivity}
Drones form a \textbf{communication graph}:
\[
G_t = (V, E_t),
\quad
E_t = \bigl\{(i,j) : \|p_i - p_j\| \le R_{\text{comm}}\bigr\}
\]

\vspace{0.5em}
\textbf{Connectivity risk} (is UAV $i$ a cut-vertex?):
\[
\text{risk}_i(t) = \mathbf{1}\!\bigl[\,G_t^{-i} \text{ is disconnected}\,\bigr]
\]

\vspace{0.5em}
\begin{block}{Why this matters}
A drone that is the \emph{only link} between two parts of the swarm
should \textbf{not} leave for charging without a replacement.
\end{block}

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Desired property:}
$G_t$ is connected $\;\forall\, t$.
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% SLIDE 10 — Battery Model
% ============================================================
\begin{frame}{Battery Model}
Three sources of energy drain:
\[
b_i(t+\Delta t) = b_i(t)
\underbrace{- \frac{P_{\text{hover}} + P_{\text{move}} + P_{\text{comm}}}{B_i^{\max}}\,\Delta t}_{\text{drain}}
+ \underbrace{\Delta b_i^{\text{charge}}}_{\text{recharge (at pad)}}
\]

\vspace{0.5em}
\textbf{Return-to-charge condition:}
\[
b_i(t) \cdot B_i^{\max}
\;\le\;
E_i^{\text{req}}
= E_i^{\text{station}} + E_i^{\text{return}} + E^{\text{reserve}}
\]

\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{tabular}{@{}ll@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Symbol} & \textbf{Meaning} \\
\midrule
$P_{\text{hover}}$ & power consumed hovering (W) \\
$P_{\text{move}}$ & power consumed moving (W) \\
$P_{\text{comm}}$ & power consumed communicating (W) \\
$B_i^{\max}$ & total battery capacity (J) \\
$E_i^{\text{station}}$ & energy to reach nearest pad \\
$E_i^{\text{return}}$ & energy to return from pad \\
$E^{\text{reserve}}$ & safety margin \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% SLIDE 11 — Charging Coordination
% ============================================================
\begin{frame}{Charging Coordination}
Multiple drones may need to charge, but pads are limited.
We solve a \textbf{min-cost assignment}.

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Decision:} $y_{is} \in \{0,1\}$ --- assign UAV $i$ to pad $s$?

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Cost:}
\[
c_{is} = \alpha\, d_{is} + \beta\, q_s + \mu\, u_i
\]

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Optimisation:}
\[
\min_{y}\; \sum_{i}\sum_{s}\; c_{is}\, y_{is}
\]

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Constraints:}
\[
\sum_{s} y_{is} \le 1 \;\;\forall\, i
\qquad(\text{each UAV} \le \text{1 pad}),
\qquad
\sum_{i} y_{is} \le 1 \;\;\forall\, s
\qquad(\text{each pad} \le \text{1 UAV})
\]

\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{tabular}{@{}ll@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Symbol} & \textbf{Meaning} \\
\midrule
$d_{is}$ & distance from UAV $i$ to pad $s$ \\
$q_s$ & queue length at pad $s$ \\
$u_i$ & urgency (battery depletion risk) \\
$\alpha, \beta, \mu$ & weights \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

Solved efficiently via the \textbf{Hungarian algorithm}.
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% SLIDE 12 — Objective Function
% ============================================================
\begin{frame}{Multi-Objective Function}
\[
\min_{\pi}\;
\mathbb{E}_{\pi}
\!\left[
\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}
\Bigl(
  \underbrace{\lambda_O\, U(t)}_{\text{under-coverage}}
  + \underbrace{\lambda_E\, E(t)}_{\text{energy waste}}
  + \underbrace{\lambda_D\, D(t)}_{\text{dead time}}
  + \underbrace{\lambda_W\, W(t)}_{\text{wasted moves}}
  + \underbrace{\lambda_R\, R(t)}_{\text{recovery}}
  + \underbrace{\lambda_C\, \text{Crit}(t)}_{\text{cut-vertex}}
\Bigr)
\right]
\]

\vspace{0.4em}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lll@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Term} & \textbf{Definition} & \textbf{Penalises} \\
\midrule
$U(t)$ & $\frac{1}{M}\sum_d \mathbf{1}[n_d{<}K]$ & sensors below $K$-coverage \\
$E(t)$ & fraction of flights w/ low battery & excessive energy drain \\
$D(t)$ & fraction of time degraded & time after a failure \\
$W(t)$ & moves that don't help coverage & wasteful repositioning \\
$R(t)$ & $\min(t_{\text{recovered}}, t_{\text{cap}})$ & time to restore coverage \\
$\text{Crit}(t)$ & fraction of active cut-vertices & connectivity fragility \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% SLIDE 13 — Constraints
% ============================================================
\begin{frame}{Safety Constraints}
At every time step $t$, for all UAVs $i$:

\vspace{0.5em}
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Speed:}
    $\|v_i(t)\| \le v_{\max}$
    
    \vspace{0.3em}
    \item \textbf{Workspace:}
    $p_i(t) \in \Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$
    
    \vspace{0.3em}
    \item \textbf{Collision avoidance:}
    $\|p_i(t) - p_j(t)\| \ge d_{\text{safe}}
    \quad \forall\, j \ne i$
\end{enumerate}

\vspace{0.5em}
\begin{block}{Hard vs Soft}
These are \textbf{hard constraints}. Violated states are prevented (action masking) or heavily penalised in the reward.
\end{block}
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% SLIDE 14 — Failure and Recovery
% ============================================================
\begin{frame}{Failure \& Recovery}
\textbf{Recovery time:} how long until coverage is restored after a failure at $t_f$:
\[
\tau_f = \inf\!\bigl\{\tau \ge 0 :
  n_d(t_f + \tau) \ge K \;\;\forall\, d \in \mathcal{M}\bigr\}
\]

\vspace{0.4em}
\textbf{Requirement:}
\[
\tau_f \le \tau_{\max}
\]

\vspace{0.5em}
\begin{block}{Reserve UAV Strategy}
Keep 1 drone in reserve with $b_i > b_{\text{threshold}}$.\\[0.2em]
When a drone fails, the reserve \textbf{immediately repositions} to fill the gap, reducing $\tau_f$.
\end{block}

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Activation:} reserve takes off when $F_t$ changes (new failure detected).
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% SLIDE 15 — MAPPO
% ============================================================
\begin{frame}{Learning Algorithm: MAPPO}
\textbf{Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimisation.}

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Actor} (per UAV):
$a_i \sim \pi_\theta(a_i \mid o_i)$

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Critic} (centralised, training only):
$V_\phi(s_t)$

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Actor loss} (PPO clipped):
\[
\mathcal{L}^{\text{actor}}(\theta)
= -\mathbb{E}_t\!\left[
  \min\!\left(
    r_t(\theta)\,\hat{A}_t,\;
    \text{clip}\bigl(r_t(\theta), 1{-}\epsilon, 1{+}\epsilon\bigr)\,\hat{A}_t
  \right)
\right]
\]
where $r_t(\theta) = \frac{\pi_\theta(a_t \mid o_t)}{\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}(a_t \mid o_t)}$,
$\hat{A}_t = R_t - V_\phi(s_t)$ (GAE).

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Critic loss:}
\[
\mathcal{L}^{\text{critic}}(\phi)
= \mathbb{E}_t\!\left[\bigl(R_t - V_\phi(s_t)\bigr)^2\right]
\]

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Training:} centralised critic sees $s_t$. \textbf{Execution:} each UAV acts on $o_i$ alone.
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% SLIDE 16 — Implementation Setup
% ============================================================
\begin{frame}{Simulation Setup}
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lll@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Parameter} & \textbf{Symbol} & \textbf{Value} \\
\midrule
Airspace & $\Omega$ & $100 \times 100 \times 30$ m$^3$ \\
Active UAVs & $N$ & 5 \\
Reserve UAVs & --- & 1 \\
IoT sensors & $M$ & 20 \\
Coverage radius & $R_{\text{cov}}$ & 15 m \\
Comm radius & $R_{\text{comm}}$ & 40 m \\
Min coverage & $K$ & 2 \\
Sim step & $\Delta t$ & 1 s \\
Max velocity & $v_{\max}$ & 5 m/s \\
Safe distance & $d_{\text{safe}}$ & 5 m \\
Battery capacity & $B^{\max}$ & 30\,000 J \\
Hover power & $P_{\text{hover}}$ & 50 W \\
Move power & $P_{\text{move}}$ & 75 W \\
Comm power & $P_{\text{comm}}$ & 10 W \\
Charge rate & $\Delta b^{\text{charge}}$ & 0.01/step \\
Discount & $\gamma$ & 0.99 \\
PPO clip & $\epsilon$ & 0.2 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% SLIDE 17 — End
% ============================================================
\begin{frame}
\begin{center}
\vspace{1.5em}
\Large\textbf{Questions?}
\end{center}
\end{frame}

\end{document}

% ============================================================
% ============================================================
%  PART 1: THE PROBLEM
% ============================================================
% ============================================================

% --- SLIDE 3: Concept ---
\begin{frame}{The Problem (Idea)}
\begin{center}
\large
\textbf{We have} $N$ \textbf{drones} flying over $M$ \textbf{ground sensors}.\\[0.6em]
\end{center}

\vspace{0.3em}
Each drone has a battery that drains. Drones can \textbf{die}.\\
Sensors need \textbf{continuous coverage} --- at least $K$ drones above each.

\vspace{0.5em}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.85]
  % ground targets
  \foreach \x in {1,3,5,7,9} {
    \fill[green!60!black] (\x,0) circle(0.2);
    \node[below, font=\tiny] at (\x,-0.25) {$q_{d}$};
  }
  % UAVs
  \foreach \x/\lab in {2/1,5/2,8/3} {
    \filldraw[fill=blue!20, draw=blue!70] (\x,2) -- ++(0.3,0) -- ++(-0.15,0.4) -- ++(-0.3,0) -- cycle;
    \node[above, font=\tiny] at (\x,2.5) {UAV \lab};
  }
  % coverage arrows
  \draw[->,dashed,red!60] (2,1.8) -- (1,0.2);
  \draw[->,dashed,red!60] (2,1.8) -- (3,0.2);
  \draw[->,dashed,red!60] (5,1.8) -- (5,0.2);
  \draw[->,dashed,red!60] (8,1.8) -- (7,0.2);
  \draw[->,dashed,red!60] (8,1.8) -- (9,0.2);
  % comm link
  \draw[<->,thick,blue!40] (2,2) -- (5,2);
  \draw[<->,thick,blue!40] (5,2) -- (8,2);
  \node[font=\scriptsize, blue!60] at (5,2.7) {communication links};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Challenge:} coordinate the drones with \emph{no central controller} so coverage never drops.
\end{frame}

% --- SLIDE 4: Math ---
\begin{frame}{The Problem (Math)}
We model the swarm as a \textbf{Dec-POMDP}:
\[
\mathcal{G} = \bigl\langle\,
  \underbrace{N}_{\text{agents}},\;
  \underbrace{\mathcal{S}}_{\text{state}},\;
  \underbrace{\{\mathcal{A}_i\}}_{\text{actions}},\;
  \underbrace{\{\mathcal{O}_i\}}_{\text{observations}},\;
  \underbrace{\mathcal{T}}_{\text{dynamics}},\;
  \underbrace{R}_{\text{reward}},\;
  \underbrace{\gamma}_{\text{discount}}
\,\bigr\rangle
\]

\vspace{0.4em}
\textbf{Objective:} find a policy $\pi$ that maximises expected cumulative reward:
\[
\max_{\pi}\;
\mathbb{E}_{\pi}
\!\left[
  \sum_{t=0}^{T} \gamma^{t}\, R_t
\right]
\]

\vspace{0.4em}
\begin{block}{What each piece means}
\begin{tabular}{@{}ll@{}}
$N$ & number of active UAV agents \\
$\mathcal{S}$ & every possible system configuration \\
$\mathcal{A}_i$ & what UAV $i$ can do (move, hover, charge) \\
$\mathcal{O}_i$ & what UAV $i$ can see locally \\
$\mathcal{T}$ & how the world transitions \\
$R$ & cooperative reward signal \\
$\gamma \in [0,1)$ & how much we value the future \\
\end{tabular}
\end{block}
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% ============================================================
%  PART 2: STATE  --  what the world looks like
% ============================================================
% ============================================================

% --- SLIDE 5: Concept ---
\begin{frame}{What Does the World Look Like? (Idea)}
Each second, the \textbf{entire system} has a snapshot:

\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Where every drone is} and how much charge it has left.
    \item \textbf{Where every ground sensor is} and whether it has enough drones above it.
    \item \textbf{Which charging pads are free} and whether any drone just died.
\end{enumerate}

\vspace{0.6em}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8, every node/.style={font=\small}]
  % UAV info boxes
  \node[draw=blue!60, fill=blue!5, rounded corners, minimum width=2.5cm, minimum height=1.2cm, align=center] at (0,1.5) {\textbf{UAV 1}\\pos, vel, bat, mode};
  \node[draw=blue!60, fill=blue!5, rounded corners, minimum width=2.5cm, minimum height=1.2cm, align=center] at (3.5,1.5) {\textbf{UAV 2}\\pos, vel, bat, mode};
  \node[draw=red!60, fill=red!5, rounded corners, minimum width=2.5cm, minimum height=1.2cm, align=center] at (7,1.5) {\textbf{UAV 3}\\pos, vel, bat, \textcolor{red}{DEAD}};
  \node[draw=green!60!black, fill=green!5, rounded corners, minimum width=2cm, minimum height=0.8cm, align=center] at (0,-0.5) {\textbf{Sensors}\\$q_1\ldots q_M$};
  \node[draw=orange, fill=orange!5, rounded corners, minimum width=2cm, minimum height=0.8cm, align=center] at (4,-0.5) {\textbf{Charging Pads}\\free / occupied};
  \node[draw=black, fill=gray!10, rounded corners, minimum width=2cm, minimum height=0.8cm, align=center] at (8,-0.5) {\textbf{Failure}\\who died};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

This snapshot is the \textbf{state} $s_t$.
\end{frame}

% --- SLIDE 6: Math ---
\begin{frame}{State Definition (Math)}
\[
s_t = \Bigl\{
  \underbrace{(p_i,\; v_i,\; b_i,\; m_i)}_{\text{UAV $i$ info}},
  \;\;
  \underbrace{(q_d)_{d=1}^{M}}_{\text{sensor positions}},
  \;\;
  \underbrace{Q_t}_{\text{charging pads}},
  \;\;
  \underbrace{F_t}_{\text{failures}}
\Bigr\}
\]

\vspace{0.5em}
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lll@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Symbol} & \textbf{Meaning} & \textbf{Range} \\
\midrule
$p_i$ & position of UAV $i$ & $(x,y,z) \in \mathbb{R}^3$ \\
$v_i$ & velocity of UAV $i$ & $\|v_i\| \le v_{\max}$ \\
$b_i$ & battery level & $[0, 1]$ (normalised) \\
$m_i$ & operating mode & \{serve, transit, charge\} \\
$q_d$ & position of sensor $d$ & fixed \\
$Q_t$ & charging pad occupancy & $\{0,1\}^S$ \\
$F_t$ & which UAVs failed & $\{0,1\}^N$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\vspace{0.4em}
\begin{block}{Key point}
During \textbf{training} the centralised critic sees all of $s_t$.
During \textbf{execution} each UAV only sees its own local observation (next slide).
\end{block}
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% ============================================================
%  PART 3: LOCAL OBSERVATION  --  what each drone sees
% ============================================================
% ============================================================

% --- SLIDE 7: Concept ---
\begin{frame}{What Can Each Drone See? (Idea)}
A drone \textbf{cannot see everything}. It only knows:

\begin{itemize}
    \item Its \textbf{own} position, velocity, battery.
    \item Which \textbf{neighbour drones} are nearby (within radio range).
    \item How many sensors are covered \textbf{in its local area}.
    \item Whether it is a \textbf{single point of failure} for connectivity.
    \item \textbf{How far} the nearest charging station is.
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.5em}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.75]
  % UAV i
  \filldraw[fill=blue!20, draw=blue!80, thick] (0,1) circle(0.35);
  \node[font=\small, blue!80] at (0,1) {$i$};
  % neighbours
  \filldraw[fill=blue!10, draw=blue!40] (-2,2) circle(0.25);
  \node[font=\tiny] at (-2,2) {neigh};
  \filldraw[fill=blue!10, draw=blue!40] (2.2,1.8) circle(0.25);
  \node[font=\tiny] at (2.2,1.8) {neigh};
  % comm range
  \draw[dashed, blue!30] (0,1) circle(2.5);
  \node[font=\tiny, blue!40] at (2.3,3.3) {radio range};
  % sensors nearby
  \fill[green!50!black] (-0.5,-1) circle(0.15);
  \fill[green!50!black] (0.8,-1.2) circle(0.15);
  \fill[green!50!black] (-1.5,-0.8) circle(0.15);
  \node[font=\tiny, green!40!black] at (0.15,-1.7) {local sensors};
  % charging station
  \node[draw=orange, fill=orange!10, rounded corners, font=\tiny, inner sep=2pt] at (3,-0.5) {charger: 40m};
  \draw[->, dashed, orange!60] (0,0.7) -- (2.7,-0.3);
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

This partial view is the \textbf{local observation} $o_i$.
\end{frame}

% --- SLIDE 8: Math ---
\begin{frame}{Local Observation (Math)}
\[
o_i = \bigl[
  \underbrace{p_i,\; v_i,\; b_i}_{\text{own state}},\;\;
  \underbrace{\mathcal{N}_i}_{\text{neighbours}},\;\;
  \underbrace{C_i^{\text{local}}}_{\text{local coverage}},\;\;
  \underbrace{\text{risk}_i}_{\text{cut-vertex?}},\;\;
  \underbrace{t_i^{\text{empty}}}_{\text{time-to-empty}},\;\;
  \underbrace{E_i^{\text{station}}}_{\text{station energy}}
\bigr]
\]

\vspace{0.5em}
\begin{tabular}{@{}ll@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Symbol} & \textbf{Meaning} \\
\midrule
$\mathcal{N}_i$ & indices of UAVs within $R_{\text{comm}}$ of UAV $i$ \\
$C_i^{\text{local}}$ & how many sensors near UAV $i$ are covered \\
$\text{risk}_i$ & $=1$ if removing UAV $i$ disconnects the swarm \\
$t_i^{\text{empty}}$ & seconds until battery hits the return threshold \\
$E_i^{\text{station}}$ & energy cost to reach the nearest pad \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\vspace{0.4em}
\begin{alertblock}{No central brain}
At execution time every UAV runs its own policy $\pi_\theta(a_i \mid o_i)$
using only $o_i$ --- no global state needed.
\end{alertblock}
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% ============================================================
%  PART 4: WHY DECENTRALISED?
% ============================================================
% ============================================================

% --- SLIDE 9: Concept ---
\begin{frame}{Why Not One Central Controller? (Idea)}
With 1 central controller choosing actions for all $N$ drones:

\begin{center}
\large
\textbf{Action space grows exponentially} with the number of drones.
\end{center}

\vspace{0.5em}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.7]
  % bar chart of action space
  \draw[->, thick] (0,0) -- (11,0) node[right, font=\scriptsize] {drones ($N$)};
  \draw[->, thick] (0,0) -- (0,5.5) node[above, font=\scriptsize] {$\log_{10}|\mathcal{A}|$};
  % bars
  \fill[blue!40] (0.5,0) rectangle (1.5,2.72);  % N=4, 625
  \node[below, font=\tiny] at (1,-0.1) {$N{=}4$};
  \node[above, font=\tiny] at (1,2.8) {$625$};
  \fill[blue!55] (2.5,0) rectangle (3.5,4.12);  % N=6
  \node[below, font=\tiny] at (3,-0.1) {$N{=}6$};
  \node[above, font=\tiny] at (3,4.2) {$15{,}625$};
  \fill[red!50] (4.5,0) rectangle (5.5,5.0);    % N=10
  \node[below, font=\tiny] at (5,-0.1) {$N{=}10$};
  \node[above, font=\tiny] at (5,5.1) {$\sim10^7$};
  \fill[red!70] (6.5,0) rectangle (7.5,5.5);    % N=20
  \node[below, font=\tiny] at (7,-0.1) {$N{=}20$};
  \node[above, font=\tiny] at (7,5.3) {$\sim10^{14}$};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Solution:} let each drone decide \emph{for itself}, using only what it can see.
\end{frame}

% --- SLIDE 10: Math ---
\begin{frame}{Decentralised Policy (Math)}
\textbf{Centralised:}
$|\mathcal{A}| = A^N$ where $A = |\mathcal{A}_i|$

\vspace{0.3em}

\textbf{Factorised (ours):} each UAV picks its own action:
\[
a_i \sim \pi_\theta(a_i \mid o_i)
\qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad
|\mathcal{A}|_{\text{eff}} = A \;\text{(per agent)}
\]

\vspace{0.5em}
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}ccccc@{}}
\toprule
$N$ & 4 & 6 & 10 & 20 \\
\midrule
Centralised & $5^4{=}625$ & $5^6{=}15{,}625$ & $\sim10^7$ & $\sim10^{14}$ \\
Decentralised & 5 & 5 & 5 & 5 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\vspace{0.4em}
\begin{block}{Trade-off}
Decentralised is tractable, but individual drones have \emph{partial information}.
The observation $o_i$ must carry enough context for good coordination.
\end{block}
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% ============================================================
%  PART 5: ACTION SPACE
% ============================================================
% ============================================================

% --- SLIDE 11: Concept ---
\begin{frame}{What Can a Drone Do? (Idea)}
Each drone picks \textbf{one action per time step}:

\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[
    node distance=0.8cm and 1.4cm,
    act/.style={rectangle, draw=blue!60, fill=blue!5, rounded corners,
                minimum height=0.8cm, minimum width=2.0cm, align=center, font=\small},
    arr/.style={-{Stealth[length=2mm]}, blue!50}
]
\node[act] (h) {Hover (stay)};
\node[act, right=of h] (ux) {Move $+x$};
\node[act, right=of ux] (uy) {Move $+y$};
\node[act, below=of h] (dx) {Move $-x$};
\node[act, right=of dx] (dy) {Move $-y$};
\node[act, right=of dy, fill=orange!15, draw=orange!60] (ch) {Charge};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

\vspace{0.4em}
\textbf{Hover:} stay in place, keep covering sensors.\\
\textbf{Move:} fly one step in a cardinal direction.\\
\textbf{Charge:} if at a pad, recharge battery.
\end{frame}

% --- SLIDE 12: Math ---
\begin{frame}{Action Space (Math)}
\[
\mathcal{A}_i = \bigl\{
  \text{Hover},\;
  {+x},\; {-x},\; {+y},\; {-y},\;
  \text{Charge}
\bigr\}, \quad |\mathcal{A}_i| = 6
\]

\vspace{0.4em}
\textbf{Movement constraint:}
\[
p_i(t+1) = p_i(t) + v_i(t) \cdot \Delta t,
\qquad \|v_i(t)\| \le v_{\max}, \quad p_i \in \Omega
\]
where $\Omega$ is the airspace boundary.

\vspace{0.4em}
\textbf{Charge action is only valid when:}
\[
\|p_i - p_s^{\text{pad}}\| \le d_{\text{charge}},
\quad Q_t[s] = 1 \;\text{(pad is free)}
\]
Otherwise the action defaults to \emph{Hover}.
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% ============================================================
%  PART 6: K-COVERAGE
% ============================================================
% ============================================================

% --- SLIDE 13: Concept ---
\begin{frame}{K-Coverage (Idea)}
\begin{block}{Rule}
Every ground sensor must have \textbf{at least $K$ drones} above it at all times.
\end{block}

\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8]
  % sensor
  \fill[green!50!black] (0,0) circle(0.25);
  \node[below, font=\small, green!40!black] at (0,-0.35) {sensor};
  % K=2 coverage
  \draw[<->, thick, blue!50] (-1.5,2) node[above, font=\small]{UAV 1} -- (0,0.3);
  \draw[<->, thick, blue!50] (1.5,2) node[above, font=\small]{UAV 2} -- (0,0.3);
  \node[font=\small] at (0,2.5) {\textbf{Covered} ($n_d = 2 \ge K{=}2$)};
  % uncovered
  \fill[red!60] (5,0) circle(0.25);
  \node[below, font=\small, red!60] at (5,-0.35) {sensor};
  \draw[<->, thick, red!50] (5,2) node[above, font=\small]{UAV 3} -- (5,0.3);
  \node[font=\small, red!60] at (5,2.5) {\textbf{Under-covered} ($n_d = 1 < K{=}2$)};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

\vspace{0.3em}
We want \textbf{zero under-covered sensors} for as much of the mission as possible.
\end{frame}

% --- SLIDE 14: Math ---
\begin{frame}{K-Coverage (Math)}
\textbf{Binary coverage} --- is UAV $i$ covering sensor $d$?
\[
x_{id}(t) = \mathbf{1}\!\bigl[\,\|p_i(t) - q_d\| \le R_{\text{cov}}\,\bigr]
\]

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Coverage count} for sensor $d$:
\[
n_d(t) = \sum_{i=1}^{N} x_{id}(t)
\]

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Coverage score} (fraction of sensors adequately covered):
\[
C(t) = \frac{1}{M}\sum_{d=1}^{M} \min\!\left(\frac{n_d(t)}{K},\; 1\right)
\]

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Under-coverage rate} (what we want to minimise):
\[
U(t) = \frac{1}{M}\sum_{d=1}^{M} \mathbf{1}\!\bigl[\,n_d(t) < K\,\bigr]
\]
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% ============================================================
%  PART 7: CONNECTIVITY
% ============================================================
% ============================================================

% --- SLIDE 15: Concept ---
\begin{frame}{Connectivity (Idea)}
Drones must \textbf{talk to each other} to coordinate.\\
Two drones can communicate if they are within radio range $R_{\text{comm}}$.

\vspace{0.4em}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8]
  % connected component
  \filldraw[fill=blue!15, draw=blue!40, dashed] (0,1) ellipse(2.5cm and 1.2cm);
  \node[above, font=\scriptsize, blue!60] at (0,2.1) {connected};
  \filldraw[fill=blue!20, draw=blue!70] (0,1) circle(0.3);
  \node[font=\tiny] at (0,1) {$1$};
  \filldraw[fill=blue!20, draw=blue!70] (1.5,1.5) circle(0.3);
  \node[font=\tiny] at (1.5,1.5) {$2$};
  \filldraw[fill=blue!20, draw=blue!70] (-1.2,0.5) circle(0.3);
  \node[font=\tiny] at (-1.2,0.5) {$3$};
  \draw[<->, thick, blue!50] (0,1) -- (1.5,1.5);
  \draw[<->, thick, blue!50] (0,1) -- (-1.2,0.5);
  % isolated drone
  \filldraw[fill=red!15, draw=red!60] (5,1) circle(0.3);
  \node[font=\tiny, red!60] at (5,1) {$4$};
  \node[above, font=\scriptsize, red!60] at (5,1.6) {isolated!};
  \draw[red!40, dashed] (5,1) circle(1.5);
  \node[font=\scriptsize, red!40] at (5,-0.7) {out of range};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

\vspace{0.3em}
If removing one drone \textbf{splits} the group, that drone is a \textbf{cut-vertex} --- high risk.
\end{frame}

% --- SLIDE 16: Math ---
\begin{frame}{Connectivity (Math)}
\textbf{Communication graph:}
\[
G_t = (V, E_t),
\quad
E_t = \bigl\{(i,j) : \|p_i - p_j\| \le R_{\text{comm}}\bigr\}
\]

\vspace{0.4em}
\textbf{Connectivity risk} --- is UAV $i$ a cut-vertex?
\[
\text{risk}_i(t) = \mathbf{1}\!\bigl[\,G_t^{-i} \text{ is disconnected}\,\bigr]
\]
where $G_t^{-i}$ is the graph with UAV $i$ and its edges removed.

\vspace{0.4em}
\begin{block}{Why this matters}
A drone that is the \emph{only link} between two parts of the swarm
should \textbf{not} leave for charging without a replacement taking its place.
\end{block}

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Desired global property:}
\[
G_t \text{ is connected} \quad \forall\, t
\]
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% ============================================================
%  PART 8: BATTERY MODEL
% ============================================================
% ============================================================

% --- SLIDE 17: Concept ---
\begin{frame}{Battery Model (Idea)}
Every drone burns energy doing three things:

\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Hovering} --- staying airborne.
    \item \textbf{Moving} --- flying to a new position.
    \item \textbf{Communicating} --- sending data to neighbours.
\end{enumerate}

\vspace{0.4em}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.85]
  % battery
  \draw[thick] (0,0) rectangle (6,1.2);
  \fill[green!50!black] (0,0) rectangle (4.2,1.2);
  \fill[yellow!70!black] (4.2,0) rectangle (5.2,1.2);
  \fill[red!60] (5.2,0) rectangle (6,1.2);
  \node[font=\small] at (2.1,0.6) {good};
  \node[font=\small] at (4.7,0.6) {low};
  \node[font=\small, white] at (5.6,0.6) {\textbf{return}};
  \node[font=\scriptsize, red!60] at (6.5,0.6) {$\leftarrow$ must go charge};
  % arrows
  \draw[->, thick] (0,-0.5) -- (6,-0.5) node[right, font=\scriptsize] {time};
  \node[font=\scriptsize, red!70] at (5.2,-1) {return threshold};
  \draw[|-, red!60, thick] (5.2,-0.3) -- (5.2,-0.7);
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

When battery hits the \textbf{return threshold}, the drone \emph{must} go charge.
\end{frame}

% --- SLIDE 18: Math ---
\begin{frame}{Battery Model (Math)}
\[
b_i(t+\Delta t) = b_i(t)
+ \underbrace{\frac{-P_{\text{hover}} - P_{\text{move}} - P_{\text{comm}}}{B_i^{\max}}\,\Delta t}_{\text{drain}}
+ \underbrace{\Delta b_i^{\text{charge}}}_{\text{recharge (at pad)}}
\]

\vspace{0.4em}
\textbf{Return-to-charge condition:}
\[
b_i(t) \cdot B_i^{\max}
\;\le\;
E_i^{\text{req}}
= E_i^{\text{station}} + E_i^{\text{return}} + E^{\text{reserve}}
\]

\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{tabular}{@{}ll@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Symbol} & \textbf{Meaning} \\
\midrule
$b_i(t)$ & normalised battery $[0,1]$ \\
$P_{\text{hover}}$ & power consumed hovering (W) \\
$P_{\text{move}}$ & power consumed moving (W) \\
$P_{\text{comm}}$ & power consumed communicating (W) \\
$B_i^{\max}$ & total battery capacity (J) \\
$E_i^{\text{station}}$ & energy to reach nearest pad \\
$E_i^{\text{return}}$ & energy to return from pad to current area \\
$E^{\text{reserve}}$ & safety margin \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% ============================================================
%  PART 9: CHARGING COORDINATION
% ============================================================
% ============================================================

% --- SLIDE 19: Concept ---
\begin{frame}{Charging Coordination (Idea)}
Multiple drones may need to charge simultaneously, but pads are limited.

\vspace{0.4em}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.7]
  % drones needing charge
  \node[draw=red!60, fill=red!10, rounded corners, font=\small] at (0,2) {UAV 1 (15\%)};
  \node[draw=red!60, fill=red!10, rounded corners, font=\small] at (3,2) {UAV 2 (8\%)};
  \node[draw=red!60, fill=red!10, rounded corners, font=\small] at (6,2) {UAV 4 (22\%)};
  % pads
  \node[draw=orange, fill=orange!15, rounded corners, font=\small] at (1,0) {Pad A};
  \node[draw=orange, fill=orange!15, rounded corners, font=\small] at (5,0) {Pad B};
  % assignment arrows
  \draw[->, very thick, green!60!black] (0,1.7) -- (1,0.4);
  \draw[->, very thick, green!60!black] (3,1.7) -- (5,0.4);
  \node[font=\small, red!60, align=center] at (6,0.8) {wait! (no pad)};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

\vspace{0.3em}
We solve a \textbf{min-cost assignment} every time a drone requests a pad.
\end{frame}

% --- SLIDE 20: Math ---
\begin{frame}{Charging Coordination (Math)}
\textbf{Decision variable:}
$y_{is} \in \{0,1\}$ \textbf{---} assign UAV $i$ to pad $s$?

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Cost:}
\[
c_{is} = \alpha\, d_{is} + \beta\, q_s + \mu\, u_i
\]
where $d_{is}$ = distance, $q_s$ = queue length at pad, $u_i$ = urgency.

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Optimisation:}
\[
\min_{y}\; \sum_{i}\sum_{s}\; c_{is}\, y_{is}
\]

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Constraints:}
\[
\sum_{s} y_{is} \le 1 \;\;\forall\, i
\qquad\text{(each UAV $\le$ 1 pad)},
\qquad
\sum_{i} y_{is} \le 1 \;\;\forall\, s
\qquad\text{(each pad $\le$ 1 UAV)}
\]

\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{tabular}{@{}ll@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Symbol} & \textbf{Meaning} \\
\midrule
$\alpha$ & weight for distance to station \\
$\beta$ & weight for station queue length \\
$\mu$ & weight for urgency (battery depletion risk) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\vspace{0.3em}
For pairwise assignment, the \textbf{Hungarian algorithm} solves this efficiently.
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% ============================================================
%  PART 10: OBJECTIVE FUNCTION
% ============================================================
% ============================================================

% --- SLIDE 21: Concept ---
\begin{frame}{The Goal (Idea)}
We are balancing \textbf{6 competing objectives}:

\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[
    node distance=0.55cm and 0.8cm,
    obj/.style={rectangle, draw=#1!60, fill=#1!8, rounded corners,
                minimum height=0.65cm, minimum width=2.2cm, align=center, font=\small}
]
\node[obj=red] (U) {Minimise\\under-coverage};
\node[obj=blue, right=of U] (E) {Minimise\\energy waste};
\node[obj=green!60!black, right=of E] (D) {Minimise\\dead time};
\node[obj=orange, below=of U] (W) {Minimise\\unnecessary moves};
\node[obj=purple, below=of E] (R) {Minimise\\recovery time};
\node[obj=cyan!70!black, below=of D] (C) {Protect\\cut-vertices};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

\vspace{0.4em}
Each objective gets a \textbf{weight} $\lambda$ to control importance.
\end{frame}

% --- SLIDE 22: Math ---
\begin{frame}{Multi-Objective Formulation (Math)}
\[
\min_{\pi}\;
\mathbb{E}_{\pi}
\!\left[
\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}
\Bigl(
  \underbrace{\lambda_O\, U(t)}_{\text{under-coverage}}
  + \underbrace{\lambda_E\, E(t)}_{\text{energy waste}}
  + \underbrace{\lambda_D\, D(t)}_{\text{dead time}}
  + \underbrace{\lambda_W\, W(t)}_{\text{wasted moves}}
  + \underbrace{\lambda_R\, R(t)}_{\text{recovery}}
  + \underbrace{\lambda_C\, \text{Crit}(t)}_{\text{cut-vertex risk}}
\Bigr)
\right]
\]

\vspace{0.4em}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lll@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Term} & \textbf{Definition} & \textbf{What it penalises} \\
\midrule
$U(t)$ & $\frac{1}{M}\sum_d \mathbf{1}[n_d{<}K]$ & sensors below $K$-coverage \\
$E(t)$ & fraction of flights with low battery & excessive energy drain \\
$D(t)$ & fraction of time in degraded state & time after a failure \\
$W(t)$ & moves that don't improve coverage & wasteful repositioning \\
$R(t)$ & $\min(t_{\text{recovered}}, t_{\text{cap}})$ & time to restore coverage \\
$\text{Crit}(t)$ & fraction of cut-vertices active & connectivity fragility \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% ============================================================
%  PART 11: CONSTRAINTS
% ============================================================
% ============================================================

% --- SLIDE 23: Concept ---
\begin{frame}{Safety Constraints (Idea)}
Drones must follow hard rules at \emph{every} time step:

\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Speed limit} --- don't fly too fast.
    \item \textbf{Stay inside} the designated airspace.
    \item \textbf{Don't collide} --- maintain safe distance from other drones.
\end{enumerate}

\vspace{0.5em}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.7]
  % airspace boundary
  \draw[thick, dashed, gray] (-1,-0.5) rectangle (9,3.5);
  \node[font=\scriptsize, gray] at (4,3.7) {airspace $\Omega$};
  % drones
  \filldraw[fill=blue!20, draw=blue!70] (2,2) circle(0.3);
  \filldraw[fill=blue!20, draw=blue!70] (4,2) circle(0.3);
  \filldraw[fill=blue!20, draw=blue!70] (6,1) circle(0.3);
  % safe distance
  \draw[<->, red!50] (2,1.4) -- (4,1.4) node[midway, below, font=\tiny, red!60] {$\ge d_{\text{safe}}$};
  % velocity arrow
  \draw[->, very thick, blue!50] (6,1) -- (7.5,1.8);
  \node[font=\tiny, blue!50] at (7.2,2.1) {$\|v\| \le v_{\max}$};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}
\end{frame}

% --- SLIDE 24: Math ---
\begin{frame}{Safety Constraints (Math)}
At every time step $t$, for all UAVs $i$:

\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Speed:}
    $\|v_i(t)\| \le v_{\max}$
    \item \textbf{Workspace:}
    $p_i(t) \in \Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$
    \item \textbf{Collision avoidance:}
    $\|p_i(t) - p_j(t)\| \ge d_{\text{safe}}
    \quad \forall\, j \ne i$
\end{enumerate}

\vspace{0.6em}
\begin{block}{Hard vs soft}
These are \textbf{hard constraints} --- violated states are either
prevented (action masking) or heavily penalised in the reward.
\end{block}
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% ============================================================
%  PART 12: FAILURE & RECOVERY
% ============================================================
% ============================================================

% --- SLIDE 25: Concept ---
\begin{frame}{What Happens When a Drone Dies? (Idea)}

\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.7]
  % before failure
  \node[font=\small] at (0,3) {\textbf{Before failure}};
  \filldraw[fill=blue!20, draw=blue!70] (0,2) circle(0.3);
  \filldraw[fill=blue!20, draw=blue!70] (1.5,2) circle(0.3);
  \filldraw[fill=blue!20, draw=blue!70] (3,2) circle(0.3);
  \draw[->, dashed, red!50] (0,1.7) -- (0,0.5);
  \draw[->, dashed, red!50] (1.5,1.7) -- (1.5,0.5);
  \draw[->, dashed, red!50] (3,1.7) -- (3,0.5);
  \fill[green!50!black] (0,0) circle(0.15);
  \fill[green!50!black] (1.5,0) circle(0.15);
  \fill[green!50!black] (3,0) circle(0.15);
  % failure arrow
  \draw[->, very thick, red!70] (4,1) -- (5,1);
  \node[font=\small, red!70] at (4,1.5) {failure!};
  % after failure
  \node[font=\small] at (7,3) {\textbf{After failure}};
  \filldraw[fill=blue!20, draw=blue!70] (6,2) circle(0.3);
  \node[font=\scriptsize] at (6,2) {$1$};
  \filldraw[fill=blue!20, draw=blue!70] (9,2) circle(0.3);
  \node[font=\scriptsize] at (9,2) {$3$};
  \node[font=\scriptsize, red!60] at (7.5,2) {\textbf{X}};
  \draw[->, dashed, red!50] (6,1.7) -- (6,0.5);
  \draw[->, dashed, red!50] (9,1.7) -- (9,0.5);
  \draw[->, dashed, red!50] (7.5,1.7) -- (7.5,0.5);
  \fill[green!50!black] (6,0) circle(0.15);
  \fill[green!50!black] (7.5,0) circle(0.15);
  \fill[green!50!black] (9,0) circle(0.15);
  \node[font=\scriptsize, red!60] at (7.5,0.4) {gap!};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

We measure \textbf{how quickly} the remaining drones close the gap.
\end{frame}

% --- SLIDE 26: Math ---
\begin{frame}{Failure \& Recovery (Math)}
\textbf{Recovery time:} how long until coverage is restored after a failure at $t_f$:
\[
\tau_f = \inf\!\bigl\{\tau \ge 0 :
  n_d(t_f + \tau) \ge K \;\;\forall\, d \in \mathcal{M}\bigr\}
\]

\vspace{0.4em}
\textbf{Requirement:}
\[
\tau_f \le \tau_{\max}
\]

\vspace{0.4em}
\begin{block}{Reserve UAV strategy}
Keep 1 drone in reserve with $b_i > b_{\text{threshold}}$.\\
When a drone fails, the reserve immediately repositions to fill the gap, reducing $\tau_f$.
\end{block}

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Reserve activation condition:}
\[
\text{reserve takes off when } F_t \text{ changes (new failure detected)}
\]
\end{frame}

% ============================================================
% ============================================================
%  PART 13: HOW THE AI LEARNS (MAPPO)
% ============================================================
% ============================================================

% --- SLIDE 27: Concept ---
\begin{frame}{How the AI Learns (Idea)}
We use \textbf{MAPPO} --- Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimisation.

\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[
    node distance=0.9cm,
    box/.style={rectangle, draw=blue!60, fill=blue!5, rounded corners,
                minimum height=0.8cm, minimum width=2.5cm, align=center, font=\small},
    arr/.style={-{Stealth[length=2mm]}, thick, blue!60}
]
\node[box] (obs) {Observation $o_i$};
\node[box, right=1.8cm of obs] (actor) {Actor $\pi_\theta$\\(choose action)};
\node[box, right=1.8cm of actor] (env) {Environment\\(simulate)};
\node[box, below=0.9cm of actor] (critic) {Critic $V_\phi$\\(estimate value)};
\node[box, below=0.9cm of env] (rew) {Reward $R$};
\draw[arr] (obs) -- (actor);
\draw[arr] (actor) -- (env);
\draw[arr] (env) -- (rew);
\draw[arr] (rew) -- (critic);
\draw[arr] (critic) -- (actor) node[midway, left, font=\scriptsize] {update};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Centralised training, decentralised execution:} during training the critic sees all of $s_t$; at deployment each drone acts on $o_i$ alone.
\end{frame}

% --- SLIDE 28: Math ---
\begin{frame}{MAPPO (Math)}
\textbf{Actor} (per UAV): $a_i \sim \pi_\theta(a_i \mid o_i)$

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Critic} (centralised, training only): $V_\phi(s_t)$

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Actor loss} (PPO clipped):
\[
\mathcal{L}^{\text{actor}}(\theta)
= -\mathbb{E}_t\!\left[
  \min\!\left(
    r_t(\theta)\,\hat{A}_t,\;
    \text{clip}\bigl(r_t(\theta), 1{-}\epsilon, 1{+}\epsilon\bigr)\,\hat{A}_t
  \right)
\right]
\]
where $r_t(\theta) = \frac{\pi_\theta(a_t \mid o_t)}{\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}(a_t \mid o_t)}$ and $\hat{A}_t = R_t - V_\phi(s_t)$ (GAE advantage).

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Critic loss:}
\[
\mathcal{L}^{\text{critic}}(\phi)
= \mathbb{E}_t\!\left[
  \bigl(R_t - V_\phi(s_t)\bigr)^2
\right]
\]

\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{tabular}{@{}ll@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Hyperparameter} & \textbf{Value} \\
\midrule
Number of UAVs $N$ & 5 \\
IoT devices $M$ & 20 \\
Discount $\gamma$ & 0.99 \\
PPO clip $\epsilon$ & 0.2 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{frame}

for i, slide in enumerate(prs.slides):
    print(f"\n--- SLIDE {i+1} ---")
    for shape in slide.shapes:
        print(f"  shape id={shape.shape_id} name={shape.name!r} type={shape.shape_type} ph={shape.is_placeholder}")
        if shape.is_placeholder:
            print(f"     ph_type={shape.placeholder_format.type} idx={shape.placeholder_format.idx}")
        # print bbox
        try:
            print(f"     pos=({shape.left},{shape.top}) size=({shape.width}x{shape.height})")
        except Exception as e:
            print("     pos err", e)
        if shape.has_text_frame:
            txt = shape.text_frame.text
            if txt.strip():
                for p in shape.text_frame.paragraphs:
                    runs = p.runs
                    line = "".join(r.text for r in runs)
                    if line.strip():
                        print(f"     TEXT: {line[:160]}")
        if shape.has_table:
            print("     TABLE:")
            for r in shape.table.rows:
                print("       " + " | ".join(c.text for c in r.cells))

from pptx import Presentation

    for sh in s.shapes:

    "Flying Ad-hoc Networks (FANETs)",

from pptx import Presentation
src = "PPT.pptx"
prs = Presentation(src)
sldIdLst = prs.slides._sldIdLst
kids = list(sldIdLst)
order = list(range(10, 15)) + list(range(0, 10))

from pptx import Presentation

    title = ""
    for ph in s.placeholders:
        if ph.placeholder_format.idx == 0 and ph.text_frame.text.strip():
            title = ph.text_frame.text.strip().replace("\n", " / ")
            break
    if not title:
        # fallback first non-empty
        for ph in s.placeholders:
            if ph.text_frame.text.strip():
                title = ph.text_frame.text.strip().replace("\n"," / ")[:60]
                break
    print(f"{i:2d}. {title[:80]}")

\section{The contract and the current state}
The work runs to 26 October 2026. The deliverable is a paper whose every number can be traced to the artefact it was measured in, and whose comparative claims are derived in code rather than asserted, so that the paper says the right thing whichever way a measurement comes out. This report is the log of that work: the protocol, the defects that were found and fixed, the audits that were run and what they changed, the measurements, and the questions that are still open.

\uavbottomrule
\end{tabularx}

\section{The measurement protocol}
The paper's numbers are produced under one protocol, and the artefacts record the protocol they were measured under:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,label=\textcolor{uavblue}{\bfseries\arabic*.},itemsep=2pt,topsep=2pt]
\item \textbf{Training}: 25 episodes of 2000 control steps per training run, and every table in the paper is a mean over 8 training runs on one device. Two tables are measured at a smaller budget and say so: the stress ablation at 6 episodes, because that scenario is hard enough that a longer run does not finish, and the map-resolution sweep at 20.
\item \textbf{Evaluation}: five scenes per policy, and the number of evaluation scenes is part of the protocol --- a run with three is a different measurement, because a per-seed row is the mean over the scenes.
\item \textbf{The device and the thread count} are part of the protocol. The floating-point kernels differ between the CPU and the GPU and the order of the reductions differs with the thread count, so two runs of the same configuration that land on different devices are not the same experiment. The device is pinned and the thread count is pinned in code.
\item \textbf{The evaluation is seeded} from the evaluation seed alone, so every controller is measured on the same random stream on the same scene --- common random numbers --- and a comparison between controllers is a comparison between policies rather than between the luck of the draw.
\item \textbf{The ablations are paired}: the variants share the training seeds, so a difference is measured on the same training runs and reported as a confidence interval on the paired difference.
\item \textbf{Inference is by interval, never by threshold}. An explanation is excluded only if the arm that tests it has an upper confidence limit below the gap; a null result is a statement about the resolution of that arm, and the resolution is reported with it.
\end{enumerate}

\label{fig:report-arms}

The arms' verdict, derived from the intervals: Controlled arms bound how much of the gap each alternative explanation can account for: adding the agent identity (upper limit 0.137, margin +0.161); the full observation of the proposed configuration (upper limit 0.102, margin +0.196); removing the energy constraint (upper limit 0.081, margin +0.217); removing the threshold term (upper limit 0.028, margin +0.270); the previous energy rule (upper limit -0.038, margin +0.336), against a gap of 0.298.  Every arm's upper limit is below the gap, so none of them can be the whole of the explanation, by margins that are small but positive.  Every interval is paired over the same training seeds, against the local-only arm A of the observation experiment and the proposed configuration of the energy experiment.

The training-budget sweep: 8 episodes: 0.595, 16 episodes: 0.621, 25 episodes: 0.662. the coverage moves by +0.067 over the range the sweep covers, which is about 22\% of the gap of 0.298, and the increments between successive budgets are +0.026, +0.041; the last of them, +0.041, is 2.8 standard errors from zero (the standard error of the difference is 0.014, paired over the same 8 training seeds), so the coverage does keep rising with the budget over the range the sweep covers.

\section{The audits, and what they changed}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.15em,itemsep=4pt,topsep=2pt,label={\color{uavblue}\scriptsize\textbullet}]
\item \textbf{Audit 1} (done): the seven load-bearing claims. Found 4 wrong as stated; all corrected.
\item \textbf{Audit 2} (done): the reward terms, the mask and the joint projection, the H-step lookahead, the energy budget, the value normalisation, the metrics, the oracle normalisation, the evaluation protocol. 25 items, 21 verified, 0 failed, 4 informational.
\item \textbf{Audit 3} (DONE, 20 Oct 23:15): the model and the results' claims. Brief: \texttt{C:\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}Users\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}gbust\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}AppData\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}Local\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}Temp\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}opencode\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}audit3\_brief.txt} (9 items). It found, and these are now fixed:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.25em,itemsep=1.5pt,topsep=2pt,label={\color{uavmuted}\scriptsize\textendash}]
\item \textbf{The central exclusion argument was OVERSTATED.} "What remains is credit assignment" is not supported by three non-detections at three training seeds: a non-detection is a statement about the arm's resolution, and a sufficiency test cannot eliminate a cause that is necessary but not sufficient. The abstract, the introduction and the conclusion now say the residual is CONSISTENT WITH the credit assignment and with several other causes the arms do not test, and that the paper does not claim to have excluded them.
\item The "loses on its own objective therefore the learning pipeline is at fault" inference was a false dichotomy -> fixed.
\item \textbf{The constrained ceiling IS 1.000}, because the oracle's construction is itself admissible under the safety filter, so the paper's claim that an informative constrained ceiling was missed was false -> fixed.
\item The hop rule constrains the MOVER's eccentricity, not the graph's diameter, and can freeze an agent in a dispersed graph -> stated.
\item The service-continuity gap separates the two controllers far more sharply than the coverage gap -> now reported beside it.
\item The spread quoted for a learned controller contains the rollout-to-rollout variation, and the cancellation of the scene component in a difference is an ASSUMPTION -> both stated.
\item \textbf{The framework's contribution needed a measurement.} On the report's own infeasible N=5 configuration the reactive heuristic still reaches CK 0.648 with full connectivity while the joint metric is 0.000 and the oracle reaches 0.990: neither metric alone distinguishes the instance from a feasible one, and it is the certificate that makes the reading decidable. Measured by \texttt{analysis/\allowbreak{}infeasible\_instance.py}, audit item I1.
\item \textbf{The rule's privileged access was an untested alternative explanation.} Now measured: \texttt{analysis/\allowbreak{}infeasible\_instance.py} aside, the arm \texttt{Reactive (local assignment)} in \texttt{train.py} runs the same rule without the global coverage state, and the verdict is derived from the measurement in the token filler.
\end{itemize}
\item \textbf{Audit 4} (DONE, 20 Oct 22:10): \textbf{the statistics of the re-measurement protocol itself.} Brief: \texttt{C:\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}Users\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}gbust\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}AppData\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}Local\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}Temp\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}opencode\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}audit4\_brief.txt}. It found the following, and all of it is now fixed:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.25em,itemsep=1.5pt,topsep=2pt,label={\color{uavmuted}\scriptsize\textendash}]
\item \textbf{The "yardstick" rule was not a test.} Comparing a component's difference with the learner's own seed-to-seed spread has a per-arm null error rate of about a third at three training seeds, and it buys no power: the measurement cannot detect a true effect of the size it flags. -> replaced by paired t intervals on the per-seed differences, and the paper says "no effect larger than X was DETECTED at this budget and this seed count" rather than "the component is inert".
\item \textbf{The negative conclusion's mechanistic half was overstated.} The arms are null results used as evidence of absence. -> the abstract, the introduction and the conclusion now state the descriptive gap with its interval, and list the claims the measurements do NOT support.
\item \textbf{The quoted uncertainty omitted the scene variance.} -> the variance is now decomposed: the seed component is the uncertainty of a comparison, the scene component is common to all controllers and cancels in every difference.
\item \textbf{The matched budget does not control for budget-conditionality or for redundancy between components.} -> the paper says so, and says a budget sweep would be needed.
\item \textbf{"A training run is deterministic given its seed" was not established.} -> now established by two tests and by audit item T1 (the seed is set BEFORE the networks are constructed, so the initialisation is seeded too).
\item \textbf{The deterministic-vs-sampled comparison.} The paper's argmax row already settles the sampling-handicap objection, and the heuristic's information advantage is now stated as a limitation.
\item The audit's recommendations NOT taken, and why: raising the seed count to 10+ (the compute does not fit the deadline, so the paper reports intervals and a resolution instead of verdicts), decoupling the scene and action streams (would need the whole matrix re-measured), and a budget sweep (same reason). Each audit gets a SELF-CONTAINED brief: the setting, the model, the measured numbers, and the exact claims to check, because a fresh subagent has no context. It is instructed to work purely mathematically (no web, no code, no repository) and to be adversarial rather than agreeable.
\end{itemize}
\item \textbf{Audit 5} (MiniMax M3.1, 21 Oct) -- the corner certificate's geometry, the packing survey, and the budget sweep's inference. Found four errors, all applied.
\item \textbf{Audit 5} (Beam Free Max, 21 Oct) -- the same three, independently. Found the same four, plus that the corner condition is sufficient and not necessary. All applied.
\item \textbf{Audit 6} (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, 21 Oct) -- sixteen overstatements in the prose against the artefacts. All applied; the serious one was the energy repair reported as a null.
\item \textbf{Deep research} (Beam Free Max, 21 Oct) -- the attributed numbers checked against their sources, the novelty claim stress-tested, and the IEEE page limits established. Song's 81.04\% and 67.07\% and Fan's 74\% are confirmed; the Luna reference was wrong and is fixed; the novelty claim survives.
\item \textbf{Audit 7} (MiniMax M3.1, 21 Oct) -- the eight-seed re-measurement checked against the raw per-seed rows, with every interval recomputed by hand. Ten findings, all applied: the budget's paired increment, two population standard deviations, a rounding disagreement between a summary and its table, the wrong rule named in a sentence, an asymmetric interval described as symmetric, a caption that said five where the table said eight, an audit claim in the abstract that was broader than the audit, an arms' sentence that did not name its reference arm, an exclusion stated without its scope, and a share whose denominator appears nowhere in the paper.
\end{itemize}

\section{Negative results, kept on the record}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.15em,itemsep=4pt,topsep=2pt,label={\color{uavblue}\scriptsize\textbullet}]
\item The \textbf{runtime instrument cannot support a path-loss cross-validation}: a transmit-power sweep shows the available per-receiver SNR statistic tracks the transmit power exactly but is independent of the receiver's distance. The equivalence is therefore established from INET's source, not from a running simulation. This is a negative control that the paper reports on itself.
\item \textbf{Phase 3 (Simu5G PHY) is scaffolded but not executed} with the learned policy.
\item \textbf{The coverage-map summary makes no measurable difference} to the coverage at any resolution tested; it changes what the policy DOES (the swarm's spread), and the paper reports that rather than dropping the feature.
\item \textbf{The thread count does not change the training run} on this workload.
\item \textbf{The reward term for the energy cost is numerically inert} at the reported weights.
\item \textbf{The credit-assignment arm does not resolve the credit assignment}: the cheapest modification in the direction the diagnosis points moves the wrong way, and the paper says so rather than claiming the diagnosis.
\item \textbf{The GPU does not accelerate this workload.} Measured, in \texttt{analysis/\allowbreak{}device\_sensitivity.json}: the GPU takes about 1.26x the CPU's wall clock for the same training run. The profile says why: the simulator is a sequential Python loop and is about 85\% of a run, the network is about 8\% of it, and on the GPU even that 8\% is several times slower in absolute terms (tiny tensors, launch overhead). The measurement is in the artefact, and the earlier claim that the choice "costs about one percent" was false and has been removed from the code and from this file.
\end{itemize}
