# Subagent 10 - Evolutionary / CEM / Black-Box Optimization (first-principles, 2026-10-30)

From ses_e76ee63e0ffeHRn7DV2UchjSU2 (Mercury 3, read-only).

## Reframed problem
LL: a controller whose per-episode CK on the fixed 5-scene protocol beats the reactive rule (0.740 single_pad; 0.716 small_battery) and is robust across seeds. Central paradox: the signal that matters is whole-episode (energy/return cycles decide coverage), yet every gradient learner converts that long-horizon signal into collapse or null credit (C3 null; BC-init PPO fell 0.818->0.45; MAPPO 0.60-0.75). PPO's failure is not representational - BC proves good policies exist in this exact network class. The failure is in the update rule, not the policy class.

## Ground truths
- [FACT] Env is deterministic given seed; eval is a function of (policy, scene), seeded and paired (repro_probe.py, README section 5).
- [FACT] bc_actor.pt (MLP 57->128->128->6, ~24.7k params) scores ~0.8-0.98; PPO fine-tune from it collapses (residual logs).
- [FACT] MAPPO-from-scratch: nominal mean 0.674, per-seed 0.60-0.75; single_pad seeds 0.36-0.75.
- [REASONED] Fitness noise is the classic ES killer; here it is near-eliminated by deterministic sim + common random numbers per seed.

## Why black-box search should win
ES/CEM optimizes exactly f(theta)=episode return - no critic, bootstrapping, value-normalization fragility (C8-class issues vanish), no gradient through rare return events. Updates are rank-based and elitist, so the incumbent can never regress below the BC start - an impossibility for the PPO that collapsed below its own init. Prior art: Salimans 2017 (ES rivals RL, long horizons, sparse rewards, scalar-only communication = perfect for 6 cores). GASS 2018 (ES/CEM solving cooperative multi-agent UAV swarm combat with sparse rewards). Drones 2024 (ES pre-training beats REINFORCE on UAV-swarm policies). Stulp & Sigaud 2012 (CEM/CMA-ES as policy-improvement backbone). Difference from closest art: evolutionary fine-tuning from a BC warm start under a strict paired-eval protocol vs a strong handwritten rule, in persistent K-coverage with charging/failure.

Full CMA-ES is infeasible at d~25k (O(d^2) covariance); use diagonal/separable CEM (O(d) memory), exactly the OpenAI-ES regime.

## Recommendation (portfolio)
- Best bet - CEM-from-BC: mean = bc_actor.pt weights; diagonal Gaussian per-layer sigma_0~0.05; lambda=48, elite mu=10, elitism, sigma halves on stagnation; fitness = team-reward sum (Eq. 28) over 1 CRN eval seed per candidate for selection; top-5 elites re-evaluated on the full 5-scene protocol; report CK/AG/SC. Action masking unchanged; trained the protocol's seeded-sampling eval (argmax degenerates under sharing).
- Cheap option - do first: evaluate the existing BC actor alone under the strict 5-scene protocol per scenario (~1 h). It may already clear the bar; sets the baseline for CEM's marginal gain.
- High-variance arm - CEM-from-scratch (larger sigma, restarts): isolates whether BC init is load-bearing or merely speed.

## Stress test / premortem
Top risks: (1) fitness noise from sampled actions swamps ranking - mitigated by CRN + same eval seed per generation; (2) sigma too small -> no gain, too large -> averages away structure - adaptive halving + elitism; (3) symmetric-observation degeneracy - agent ID already in obs; (4) CEM finds a local optimum above BC but below rule - that is the falsification case.

## TEST (cheapest decisive)
Scenarios: single_pad, then small_battery. 30 generations, lambda=48, 6 parallel workers (~6-8 h, same scale as existing runs). Success: best-elite median CK on the 5-scene protocol >= 0.78 AND >= BC-init CK + 0.03, with AG/SC not below the rule's.

## KILL RULE
Kill after 30 generations if best-elite median CK < max(rule CK, BC CK + 0.03); or if no elite exceeds BC-init fitness by one eval-spread by generation 10; or if elitism still regresses (harness bug).

## CONFIDENCE
- [FACT] Deterministic paired eval; BC scores; PPO collapse; MAPPO spread - all read from artefacts.
- [REASONED] ES/CEM avoids the exact failure modes observed (critic/credit/value fragility): Salimans 2017, GASS 2018, Drones 2024.
- [SPECULATIVE] A >=0.03 improvement over BC via <=30 generations of fine-tuning is achievable - precisely what TEST falsifies.
- Sources: Salimans et al. 2017 (ES), GASS 2018 (cooperative UAV swarm), Drones 2024 (ES pre-training), Stulp & Sigaud 2012 (CEM/CMA-ES as policy improvement).

# Subagent 1 - Paper Thesis Reframe (first-principles, 2026-10-30)

From ses_e770378a9ffeaFRMbc0H9t912n (Mercury 3, read-only).

## Reframed thesis

The paper's defensible core is a rigorous feasibility certification of MARL for persistent K-coverage, not a performance win:

> Under a pre-registered, converged, 5-seed protocol with a certified network-in-the-loop simulator, a hand-designed reactive rule equals or beats MAPPO in all five stress regimes (best case: tie in multi-failure, delta = -0.003; otherwise rule wins by 0.09-0.35 CK), and the residual gap to the oracle ceiling is governed by coverage/energy geometry, not communication.

Inverts "learning beats rule" into "certifying where learning does NOT help, and why."

## Surviving / dropped contributions

Survives (rebuilt):
- C1 network certificate -> reframed as a NEGATIVE scope result: at 80 m, PDR ~0.998, range margin 22x, so network is not the binding constraint. Network-realism is not where headroom lives.
- C4 evaluation methodology -> becomes the CENTERPIECE making negative results trustworthy (pre-registration, converged budgets, headroom gate, rliable IQM, disjoint train/tune/test). Precedent: Henderson et al. 2018, Jordan et al. 2020.
- NEW positive mechanism finding: stress regimes prevent the entropy collapse that kills nominal MAPPO (collapse at ep 675; none under stress).

Dropped / demoted:
- C3 credit -> report as null result (p=0.66/0.68), not a headline.
- Residual MAPPO -> cautionary negative: BC-init strong alone (CK 0.8-0.9) but PPO fine-tuning drives entropy to 0, degenerate CK=0.4500.
- C2 topology-conditioned model -> never run; move to future work, not a contribution.

## Proposed outline (6 pages IEEE)

1. Introduction - feasibility certification + null-result study; scope boundary up front.
2. System model - Dec-POMDP, K-coverage, charging, failure, connectivity; packing bound N>=4K.
3. Evaluation methodology (C4) - pre-registration, converged budgets, headroom gate, rliable, disjoint splits. Headline: all 5 regimes pass headroom gate (ceiling - best rule >= 0.10).
4. Network-realism certificate (C1) - OMNeT++/INET co-sim, PDR(d) model, network not binding (PDR 0.998 @ 80 m; 22x range margin).
5. Main result - MAPPO vs reactive rule, 5 regimes: rule >= MAPPO in 4/5, tie in multi-failure. Table: rule 0.68-0.74; MAPPO 0.37-0.71.
6. Mechanism diagnosis - entropy collapse, stress preventing collapse, residual degeneracy, C3 null.
7. Discussion/related work - where learning could still matter (larger swarms, network-bound regimes, long-horizon delayed effects).
8. Conclusion.

Abstract headline numbers: rule wins/tie in 5/5 regimes; residual MAPPO degenerate at 0.4500; C3 p=0.66; network PDR 0.998; stress eliminates collapse.

## Risks

1. Reviewer rejects "negative result as contribution" -> lead with C4 methodology, precedent citations, one clean falsifiable claim with scope boundary, "where learning still wins" section.
2. Baseline unfairness (rule has ideal info vs learner partial) -> publish rule fully, tune under same protocol, state information advantage, add fair-information variant.
3. Generalizability overreach (single simulator) -> frame as certification case study at defined operating point; anchor with packing bound; bound C1 to studied scale (N=16, one channel, 0.1s interval).

# Subagent 2 - Algorithm Proposal (first-principles, 2026-10-30)

From ses_e770378a7ffe8r56wiPA2wT39u (Mercury 3, read-only).

## Reframe
Goal: a controller whose time-averaged K-coverage exceeds 0.74 (single_pad) / 0.716 (small_battery), on same 2000-step episodes. Central paradox: hand rule already near ceiling (oracle ~1.0, headroom 0.29-0.63); simulator near-deterministic and geometry-driven, so pure learning has little to discover and everything to destroy. Binding difficulty is stability near a strong solution, not acquisition.

## Key facts
- Charging and serve->return are physics-forced (env.py 1125-1142): the policy does not decide when to return, only where to fly. Action relevance mostly spatial allocation.
- BC alone scores 0.8-0.9; PPO fine-tuning crashes to CK=0.45 with entropy->0. A good policy exists and is destroyed by PPO. Highest-information result in repo.
- C3 per-agent credit null (p~0.66/0.68) -> credit assignment likely not the binding bottleneck.
- Performance strictly bounded by action mask (connectivity/energy/articulation); rule and learner share it, so gap is control quality, not feasibility.
- ASSUMPTION: the rule's edge partly stems from information privilege (global uncovered set). Compare learned policies to reactive_local, not global reactive, else comparison conflates info asymmetry with control.
- UNKNOWN: whether entropy-collapse is root cause or symptom of noisy critic under 400k steps (PREREG target 2e6).

## Failure modes
- Fine-tuning with tiny entropy bonus (ent_coef=0.01) lets policy trust noise-degraded value estimates -> degenerate fixed schedule.
- Team reward + shared actor -> all agents imitate each other (symmetric action collapse).
- 2000-step horizon concentrates credit in critic that must predict joint-state dependence, injecting noise into every advantage.

## Candidates
A. KL-anchored residual fine-tuning (RECOMMENDED): keep BC policy as reference pi_BC; add forward-KL trust region (or line-searched KL cap) + explicit entropy floor when fine-tuning with PPO. ANCHOR/KL-anchored offline->online recipe; documented fix for RLFT entropy collapse. Assumes collapse is binding failure and good behavior already in pi_BC. Cost: small change to MAPPO.update + reuse bc_actor.pt; ~1h/seed. Falsifier: if hard KL cap cannot hold entropy > 0.2 or CK >= 0.75, the anchor itself is faulty.

B. Value decomposition (QMIX/VDN/QTRAN): factorized joint value gives per-agent advantage. Assumes coordination bottleneck - but C3 null suggests otherwise. Cost: new learner + off-policy replay, sample-hungry, more engineering. Falsifier: if A beats reactive, B dominated; if A fails, B worth a run.

C. Model-predictive lookahead (CEM over joint actions using exact simulator): env deterministic and fully known; rollouts directly optimize coverage gain. Assumes model fidelity and acceptable compute. Cost: 8 agents x ~6 actions per step with SINR/connectivity physics -> dominates runtime. Falsifier: if perfect-model MPC also cannot beat reactive, reactive is near-optimal under the mask and there is nothing to learn. Useful as ceiling probe, not primary claim.

## Recommendation: Candidate A
Justification: targets empirically confirmed failure (PPO destroying a policy that already beats reactive), reuses existing assets, cheapest, and the only candidate whose success directly converts "BC >= reactive" into "learned >= reactive". B lost on evidence (C3 null) and cost; C is a planning benchmark, not a learning result.

## Cheapest falsifiable test
- Hypothesis: KL-anchored (forward-KL capped, entropy floor) PPO fine-tuning of bc_actor.pt holds CK >= 0.78 and ends entropy > 0.2 on single_pad, beating reactive_local.
- Setup: single_pad, 5 seeds, 200 ep x 2000 steps (~1h/seed, parallelizable ~1h wall on 6 cores).
- Success: mean CK >= 0.78 and entropy > 0.2; superiority over reactive/reactive_local via paired per-seed comparison.
- Kill rule: if by episode 100 CK < 0.75 or entropy < 0.1, stop -> falsifies collapse-as-bottleneck; escalate to B or C. Same 5 seeds for clean A vs rule comparison.

# Subagent 3 - Novelty & Positioning Audit (first-principles, 2026-10-30)

From ses_e770378a4ffe7LTySeXP3Rqcp2 (Mercury 3, read-only). URLs verified live.

## Verified landscape
- TAG-MAPPO (arXiv 2602.10029): real. Topology-aware graph MAPPO, 3D UAV aerial-ground networks under node failure; graph attention + permutation-invariant random observation shuffling; self-healing restores >90% coverage in 15 steps; ~50% fewer handoffs. Positive result.
- Fan et al., "Communication-Aware MARL for Decentralized Cooperative UAV Deployment" (DroneConnect, arXiv 2603.16141): real, SINGLE CLOSEST THREAT. Graph-based MARL under CTDE, partial observability, intermittent P2P connectivity as SNR-threshold connectivity graph conditioned on channel model; compares against MILP offline oracle upper bound; +12% coverage over MAPPO.
- CALF (arXiv 2603.12543): real but mis-framed in NOVELTY.md - general Communication-Aware Learning Framework for Distributed RL (training under delay/jitter/packet-loss), not coverage MARL with failure. Closest textual match to "train under network models" but not UAV/K-coverage specific.
- RayNet (arXiv 2302.04519): OMNeT++ + Ray/RLlib platform (infrastructure, not a verdict).
- Isaac-Net / "Network-in-the-Loop at Scale" (arXiv 2610.02370, Oct 2026): explicitly occupies the term "network-in-the-loop" (GPU-batched 5G NR for massively parallel robot learning).
- FlyNetSim (arXiv 1808.04967): ns-3 + ArduPilot, no RL loop.

## Novelty verdict per contribution
- C1 (network-in-the-loop, OMNeT++/INET co-sim): Incremental as platform (RayNet, Isaac-Net exist). Novelel as verdict: certifying ideal-observation assumptions hold at 80 m scale (PDR 0.9975, 22x margin, MAC contention negligible) is a real, defensible negative/sanity result. "Network-in-the-loop" brand is taken (Isaac-Net).
- C2 (topology-conditioned information model + training): NOT novel / weak. Fan et al. (SNR-threshold connectivity graph) and TAG-MAPPO already live in this space.
- C3 (redundancy/criticality credit): NOT supported; own data show no significant gain (p~0.66/0.68). Retract as headline.
- C4 (feasibility certification evaluation: packing bound + oracle ceiling + headroom gate + rliable): THE GENUINELY NOVEL CONTRIBUTION. "Oracle ceiling / headroom" language circulates in LLM evals but not as formal feasibility + significance gating method for MARL coverage with energy/failure constraints. Combined with honest null result, publishable and hard to scoop.

## Recommended positioning & venue
Lead with C4 + honest null result. Story: "a disciplined method for deciding whether a MARL coverage result is meaningful (packing-bound feasibility, oracle ceiling, headroom gate, rliable stats), applied to UAV-IoT K-coverage where an INET co-simulation certificate proves radio is not binding, and converged MARL variants do not beat a well-tuned reactive rule."

Venues in order:
1. IEEE INFOCOM / WCNC / Globecom (INFOCOM stretch, WCNC achievable)
2. IEEE IoT-J (fast, tolerant of honest framing)
3. ML venue/workshop (ICML/NeurIPS RL-Evaluation/AI4Sys) if re-centered on method.

Do NOT target pure ML conference on strength of C1-C3.

## Top novelty threats & differentiation
1. Fan et al. (2603.16141): same graph/communication-aware MARL + oracle-upper-bound comparison but POSITIVE result. Differentiate: (a) we certify via OMNeT++/INET packet-level realism, not analytical SINR graph; (b) persistent K-coverage with battery/recharging/failure reserve; (c) our oracle is a provable packing/ceiling bound, and headline is verified null result, not a 12% gain.
2. TAG-MAPPO (2602.10029): topology-aware resilience, positive self-healing. Differentiate: learned policies fail to beat tuned rule under energy/failure stress; casts doubt on transferability of such claims.
3. CALF (2603.12543) + Isaac-Net (2610.02370): they show training under network models helps in their settings. Differentiate: in OUR certified regime network is provably not binding, so communication-aware training cannot help - cleaner falsifiable claim.

## Proposed title + abstract
Title: "Certifying Feasibility and Reporting Null Results for Fault-Tolerant Persistent K-Coverage MARL: An OMNeT++/INET Network Certificate"

Abstract: MARL is widely claimed to solve persistent K-coverage with UAV-IoT swarms under energy, charging, and failure constraints. We ask a prior question: is the problem even feasible, and are the simulation's information assumptions valid, such that an RL comparison is meaningful? We contribute (i) a feasibility-certification evaluation: packing bound, oracle ceiling, headroom gate, and rliable statistics that decide whether an RL result is analytically possible and statistically non-degenerate; and (ii) a network certificate from OMNeT++/INET co-simulation showing at 80 m mission scale IEEE 802.11 radio is not the binding constraint (PDR 0.9975, ~22x range margin). Under this certified regime, converged MAPPO and its credit-assignment, behavior-cloning, and topology/communication-aware variants do not beat a well-tuned reactive rule; stress regimes merely prevent collapse. The contribution is not a better learner but a falsifiable method for knowing when coverage-MARL results are meaningful, plus a rigorously supported null result.

# Subagent 6 - Multi-Objective/Pareto (first-principles, 2026-10-30)

From ses_e76ee63e7fferTcBCjFyc7Zvu8 (Mercury 3, read-only).

## Reframed problem
Goal: learned decentralized policy whose CK beats reactive rule (0.7402 single_pad, 0.7162 small_battery). Central paradox: coverage-seeking, energy-conservation, connectivity-maintenance actions conflict; single scalar reward forces one fixed tradeoff, so gradient conflicts erase the coverage signal exactly where it matters.

## Ground truths & evidence
- Reward is one weighted sum of 7 terms (env.py L1280-1309): lam_O=1.0, lam_D=2.0 on a binary D_t, lam_C=0.5, lam_E=0.1, lam_W=0.05, lam_B=0/2.0. Rare binary events at weight 2.0 dominate the shared return -> high-variance GAE -> CK swings 0.23-0.90 within a seed (G1_memo).
- Residual MAPPO (BC init + PPO) collapses to entropy exactly 0.000 and identical degenerate CK=0.450 (NEGATIVE.md): scalar gradient actively walks policy off high-coverage Pareto region.
- Headroom gate passes (oracle 0.26-0.63 above rule): rule is not optimal, room exists.
- Small_battery worst gap (0.346): regime where scalar energy-vs-coverage tradeoff is tightest.

## Proposal: two orthogonal levers
(A) Fix misalignment/delay (cheap): r_t = -lam_O*U_t - lam_D*D_t - lam_R*R_t - lam_C*Crit_t - lam_B*B_t - lam_W*W_tilde, with W_tilde = W_t only if min_i(E_i - E_req_i) > 0 (never punish movement that may be maintenance), lam_B = 1.0.

(B) Potential-based shaping (PBRS; Ng et al. 1999, Devlin/Kudenko 2011 for MARL): Phi_i(s) = kappa_E*clip((E_i - E_req_i)/E_req_i, 0, 1)*1[E_i >= E_req_i] + kappa_P*(1 - d_i,pad/D_max)*1[E_i < E_req_i]. r_i^shaped = r_t + gamma*Phi_i(s') - Phi_i(s), with Phi_i = 0 at terminal/truncated states. State-based, optimum preserved. Each agent's potential uses its own battery/position, breaking the symmetry that prevents specialization.

(C) Curriculum: Phase 1 coverage skill (near-infinite battery, no failures, 2 pads); Phase 2 energy skill (restore B_max, enable A+B); Phase 3 full stress (1 pad + failures). Gate phases on eval CK plateaus; keep entropy floor (masked entropy >=0.3).

## Why it should work
A removes anti-charge gradient and activates dense immediate shortfall signal. B converts 1000-step-delayed decision into per-step telescoping gradient and gives each UAV distinguishable potential (fixes credit + symmetry). C prevents cold-start joint failure (deployment+energy+contention), the collapse mode seen in every PPO variant.

## TEST
A vs current MAPPO and reactive rule; 5 seeds, 200x2000 steps, single_pad and small_battery; paired per-seed comparison. Success: mean CK >=0.76 both regimes.

## KILL RULE
Pre-registered. Kill shaping arm if A does not beat seed-matched MAPPO by >=+0.05 in BOTH regimes (paired t, p<0.05). Kill B if fails to beat A by >=0.03. Then conclude gap is optimization (entropy), not reward structure, pivot to curriculum+entropy-floor or report null.

## CONFIDENCE
- [FACT: repo code] W_t anti-charge, lam_B=0, E_t scale, C3 marginal-coverage mechanism.
- [FACT: measured logs] entropy collapse, BC->PPO degeneracy.
- [FACT: sourced] PBRS optimality preservation; curriculum precedent in UAV MARL.
- [REASONED: untested] energy-timing dominates stress regimes; staged A->B->C separates it.
- [UNKNOWN] whether A alone suffices; hence cheapest-first ordering.
- Sources: arXiv:2202.12028 (evolutionary MORL UAV MEC, Pareto set), arXiv:2601.14092 (attention-MORL UAV-IoT data/energy tradeoff), arXiv:2410.19372 (MGDA++ strong-Pareto MARL), arXiv:2610.35736 (objective-wise counterfactual credit MOMARL), ICLR 2025 reward-dimension-reduction.

# Subagent 7 - Hierarchical RL / Options (first-principles, 2026-10-30)

From ses_e76ee63e6ffeb4p3quDjz5x8Wm (Mercury 3, read-only).

## Reframed problem
Learned MARL must beat handwritten reactive rule on CK (0.74/0.716) without collapsing. Central paradox: decisions that matter (when to leave coverage, target which deficit, when to return) are long-horizon and coupled to per-step motor choice, so flat PPO drowns sparse return signal in 2000 noisy primitive actions.

## Ground truths
- Env already runs a hard mode machine (0 serve / 1 return / 2 charge, env.py L198, L1138-1142) and rule's modes are exactly these: cover, return, charge (train.py L391-416). Threshold = pad_energy + E_reserve (L483) [FACT: code].
- Observations already expose mode, pad bearing, 4x4 deficit map, charging wait, agent id (L873-963). Actions are 6 primitives; no macros [FACT: code].
- C3 credit null; residual PPO (BC init) smokes at 0.792 then collapse risk; BC alone reaches 0.8-0.98 [FACT: docs/FINDINGS.md].

## Constraint ledger (decisive rows)
- Rule's mode structure is a fence: it separates deploy/refuel/idle sensibly. Keep it; attack only transitions.
- Rule is greedy-Markovian: returns at fixed energy threshold regardless of pad contention (2 pads, 8 UAVs), failures, future deficits. This is exploitable headroom [ASSUMPTION: untested, low cost to test].

## Representation shift
Compress time. Replace "policy over 6 primitives at every step" with policy over 3 options chosen at SMDP decision points, each option executed by frozen intra-option skill. Splits Dec-POMDP into learnable high level (mode timing/targeting) and low level (motor skills) that is NOT fine-tuned - sidestepping PPO-collapse entirely.

## Portfolio (mechanisms)
1. HIGH-LEVEL ONLY (best bet): freeze rule's own cover/return/charge movement code as options; train only MAPPO option-selector (3 actions, CTDE, existing centralized critic, existing masks/seeding, warm-started from rule's transition policy). Isolates "can learned transitions beat hand-coded ones?" - sharpest falsifiable question. Prior art: option-critic (Sutton 1999), DOC (AAMAS 2020), MADDPOC (arXiv:2112.10630, UAV charging, continuous low-level; differs: we freeze discrete low-level and benchmark vs handwritten rule).
2. BC-SKILLS (high-variance): swap low-level skills for existing BC actor (0.8-0.98 evidence) - only after (1) proves transitions matter.
3. Threshold-sweep probe (cheap): sweep E_reserve/deferral on rule; bounds greedy-timing headroom before any training.

## Why it should work
(a) Options compress 2000-step credit to ~20-50 option decisions - return event's advantage attaches to one logit instead of 300 smeared primitives; (b) peer non-stationarity absorbed at option boundaries (high level sees modes directly); (c) frozen BC skills preserve proven >0.8 low level, so PPO never touches what works; (d) env already ships every high-level signal selector needs.

## TEST
H: learned option transitions beat rule's threshold transitions. Minimal: option-wrapper around baseline_reactive internals + 3-action high-level MAPPO; same 200ep x 2000 steps x 5 seeds, both regimes, seeded eval. Success: paired mean CK gain > +0.02 (95% CI excluding 0) both regimes, no collapse.

## RECOMMENDATION
Run (1) first: frozen rule-skills + learned MAPPO option-selector. Reuses existing baseline/runtime code, one extra small policy, identical budget. If wins, upgrade skills via (2); if threshold sweep (3) already caps rule, proceed with (1) anyway - learned transitions can anticipate, not just re-threshold.

## TEST
Implement option_selector (3 logits) over frozen rule-skill options; warm-start from rule's own mode-flip policy; MAPPO at SMDP level with existing critic/masks; paired 5-seed eval vs rule on single_pad and small_battery.

## KILL RULE
If mean CK(selector) - CK(rule) <= +0.02 with paired CI spanning 0 on both regimes after 200 episodes, or entropy -> 0 / CK < 0.5 in last-10 on >=2/5 seeds, hierarchy in this form does not rescue: kill this angle (keep BC-residual separate).

## CONFIDENCE
Options compress credit and improve sample efficiency: [reasoned, sourced - Sutton 1999; DOC; MADDPOC]. Learned transitions beating greedy threshold: [speculative - precisely what TEST measures]. BC-as-skill quality: [FACT: docs, eval-mode confound unresolved]. PPO collapse is low-level, avoidable by freezing: [hypothesis; residual smoke 0.792 consistent]. Env supports test: [FACT: code]. Overall beats rule: 0.35-0.45; mechanism addresses diagnosed failures: 0.8. Reversible: no new physics, one policy, one week.

# Subagent 8 - Offline RL / Batch RL (first-principles, 2026-10-30)

From ses_e76ee63e4ffe1nbVVsHvkk6Rpx (Mercury 3, read-only).

## Reframed problem
Value sought: a learned controller whose CK reliably beats the handwritten reactive rule (0.740/0.716) under the project's own protocol (200 eps x 2000 steps, 5 seeds, CK). Central paradox: the data already contains a better-than-rule controller - BC extracts ~0.8-0.98 - but any online optimization (PPO/MAPPO) destroys it (residual seed4 log: CK 0.862 at ep 0 -> 0.450 at ep 199). The binding constraint is not credit assignment (C3 null) or reward design; it is on-policy distributional drift.

## Ground truths
1. The rule is a deterministic, decentralized policy; its behavior is reproducible and cheap to roll out. 2. The simulator is seeded and deterministic; dataset generation is exact and repeatable. 3. Offline RL with in-sample constraints provably never evaluates OOD actions (IQL, ICLR 2022; ICQ-MA, NeurIPS 2021), eliminating the drift that kills PPO.

## Constraint ledger (rows that changed the answer)
- Existing bc_data.pkl is (obs, action) pairs only - no r, s' - so it cannot train any TD method. [verified, collect_bc_data.py] -> must regenerate a full-transition dataset.
- Actions are discrete (6), 8 agents, shared params: cheap independent-per-agent critics fit the existing architecture. [verified]
- C3 credit null (per-agent actor + local critic changed nothing) means a per-agent, shared-parameter offline scheme is not a priori crippled. [verified; corrected as assumption]
- OMAR (ICML 2022): naive MA-CQL degrades with agent count; CFCQL (NeurIPS 2023) and ICQ-MA are agent-count-insensitive. [sourced]

## Portfolio (by mechanism)
- A. IQL-Ind (recommended): per-agent IQL with shared params; expectile V per agent, in-sample Q targets, policy extraction by advantage-weighted regression. Never queries OOD actions; extraction is weighted BC within support, so it cannot diverge like PPO. Outperforms BC when the dataset supports stitching (high-value segments from rule variants + BC rollouts).
- B. ICQ-MA / CFCQL as theory-stronger alternatives if stitching needs a joint value (mixer/counterfactual conservatism). Higher implementation cost.
- C. Dataset + mode-robust BC (control): explicitly models the rule's multimodal target selection (round-robin), which plain cross-entropy averages into blended bad actions.
- D. Baseline: BC (already trained), reactive rule, MAPPO, residual-PPO.

## Recommendation
Train A (IQL-Ind) on a frozen dataset of full transitions: (s, a, r, s') collected from the rule across regimes (nominal, single_pad, small_battery) and 5 seeds under the 2000-step protocol, plus epsilon-perturbed BC rollouts for coverage (~30 min/seed at 231 steps/s, parallelizable). Rationale: BC proves the rule's behavior is learnable and already above the rule; offline RL adds (i) self-selection across modes instead of mean-mode averaging and (ii) segment stitching across behavior policies - with zero online drift. Worst case it degrades to BC, which still beats the rule if the BC numbers replicate under the full protocol.

## Stress test
Premortem risks: (1) dataset too narrow -> IQL ~= BC, safe but no gain; (2) long-horizon Q variance -> keep batch norm/double Q, evaluate on 5 eval scenes; (3) failure/recovery events rare in data -> oversample failure-rich episodes during collection. Rival hypothesis: BC's 0.8-0.98 may not replicate under the 2000-step energy-binding protocol (BC was trained on 500-step data) - hence BC must be re-run under the exact protocol as a control. [ASSUMPTION: cheap to test]

## TEST (pre-registered, R2/R4/R5)
Hypothesis: IQL-Ind CK > BC CK + 0.02 and > rule CK + 0.03 (paired CI excluding 0). Minimal test: 1 seed, 1 regime, collect D, train IQL-Ind, sanity-check in-sample Q vs empirical discounted returns (corr > 0.9) and eval CK >= BC CK - 0.01 (~1-2 h). Full test: 5 seeds, frozen D, same seeded eval scenes as MAPPO runs; report IQM + paired CI.

## KILL RULE
If full-run IQL-Ind mean CK <= BC CK (CI covers 0): offline-RL improvement is dead - ship BC alone (validated under protocol). If IQL-Ind CK < rule CK - 0.02: the entire "learned beats rule" thesis fails via this route; stop and report.

## CONFIDENCE
- [verified] PPO collapse from BC init (residual log); rule dataset lacks r/s'; rule CK values.
- [sourced] IQL, ICQ-MA, CQL, CFCQL, OMAR results.
- [ASSUMPTION] stitching headroom exists in this environment (cost to test: low - it is the primary comparison).
- [reasoned] AWR extraction cannot diverge like PPO because it only regresses onto in-support actions; tagging as hypothesis, not fact.
- Sources: IQL (ICLR 2022, arXiv:2010.06213), ICQ-MA (NeurIPS 2021), OMAR (ICML 2022), CFCQL (NeurIPS 2023).

# Subagent 9 - Neuro-Symbolic / Rule-Augmented Learning (first-principles, 2026-10-30)

From ses_e76ee63e2ffeOJBridePTNW0U8 (Mercury 3, read-only).

## Reframed problem
Outcome: a controller whose CK beats the reactive rule (0.740 single_pad, 0.716 small_battery) reproducibly. The mechanism is not the goal. Paradox: supervision copies the rule (BC 0.79-0.98) but RL continuation destroys it (entropy -> exactly 0, degenerate fixed schedule, CK ~0.45, docs/NEGATIVE.md), while from-scratch MAPPO stalls at 0.37-0.71. So: keep the rule as an executable anchor, learn only where to deviate.

## Ground truths
(1) Feasible policy exists: the rule itself scores 0.740/0.716; oracle ceiling 1.0, headroom ~0.26 [FACT: results_main.csv, FINDINGS.md]. (2) Discrete 6-action space: additive real residuals (classic RPL) don't apply; the discrete analogue is Bernoulli gating over rule vs learned action. (3) BC reaches rule-level skill from the existing 11-feature observation, so the rule class is imitable [FACT: NEGATIVE.md].

## Ledger
[FACT] BC+PPO collapses (measured). [ASSUMPTION] Collapse is unanchored exploitation under 200 episodes, not credit (C3 null weakly rules credit out). [ASSUMPTION] Rule suboptimality is localized: contention, return timing, failure reconfiguration.

## Portfolio
- Baseline: full-network MAPPO (fails), BC+PPO (fails), rule (0.74).
- M1 (best bet) Rule-anchored gating. Policy = Bernoulli gate g_o(g_i) choosing baseline_reactive_local's precomputed action or a learned deviate head. Init g -> follow rule (p=0.9), BC warm-start both heads off rule rollouts, then PPO. Floor: if g collapses to always-rule, CK = 0.74 >= all MAPPO runs. Prior art: RPL (Silver et al., arXiv:1812.06298) with non-differentiable base; deterministic-high-level/DRL-low-level UAV swarm (PMC10648592).
- M2 (cheap) Threshold tuning. CEM/random search over 6-10 rule parameters (return threshold, local radius, tie-break). If a tuned rule beats 0.74, the win exists without neural nets; tells us if learning is needed at all.
- M3 (high-variance) Differentiable soft decision tree as gate (Silva et al. PMLR 2020; Distill2Explain 2024), leaves = {rule, deviate}, BC pretrain then KL-anchored PPO; interpretable (VIPER-style extraction, Bastani et al. NeurIPS 2018).

## Why M1 should work
It converts "learn a complete controller from sparse noisy reward" into "learn rare local corrections to a known-good base". Gradient signal fires only where the rule errs; the base supplies long-horizon competence. Entropy-collapse becomes benign: worst case equals the rule, which already beats MAPPO. The observation already contains pad bearing, deficit map, identity, battery [FACT: AUTONOMOUS_STATE.md], so the gate has its inputs.

## Stress test
Risks: gate never fires (result: equality); override under value-noise (degrade); corrections unlearnable in budget. Mitigations: paired eval, common random numbers, capped deviation-rate schedule, entropy floor + KL anchor.

## Cheapest test
Reuse env/train/eval; wrap env to call baseline_reactive_local for rule branch (exists). 200 episodes x 2000 steps, 5 seeds, single_pad + small_battery, paired deltas on identical eval scenes. Run M2 in parallel (one day).

RECOMMENDATION: M1 rule-anchored gate as best bet; M2 as parallel control to test whether learning is even required.
TEST: H: CK(gate) > CK(rule). Success: paired 95% CI on Delta excludes 0 with mean Delta >= +0.03, gate usage 2-50%, end-entropy > 0.3.
KILL RULE: Stop if Delta <= +0.01 (CI includes 0), or CK(gate) < CK(rule) - 0.02, or usage < 2% with no improvement; report anchored-floor result and pivot to M2-only.
CONFIDENCE: rule/MAPPO/BC/collapse numbers [FACT: measured in repo]; RPL, soft-tree, programmatic-policy lines exist [FACT: web-verified]; gating beats rule within budget [ASSUMPTION: untested]; collapse mechanism [ASSUMPTION].
- Sources: RPL (Silver et al., arXiv:1812.06298), deterministic-high-level/DRL-low-level UAV swarm (PMC10648592), Silva et al. PMLR 2020, Distill2Explain 2024, Bastani et al. NeurIPS 2018.

\subsection{Innovations: closing the small-battery and spread-start gaps}
\label{sec:results_innov}

The base configuration's learner beats the rule by $+0.029$; the stress
table shows it loses on two regimes.  The innovations below target those two.

\begin{table}[t]
\caption{Innovation ablation on the small-battery regime (zero-shot, 10 held-out
scenes).  Anchor is the corrected learner (ego+shape) evaluated on the same
regime.}
\label{tab:innov_smallbat}
\centering
\scriptsize
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccc@{}}
\toprule
configuration & CK & sd & n seeds \\
\midrule
anchor (ego+shape) & 0.765 & -- & 5 \\
+ curriculum + energy shaping + R\&F & 0.831 & 0.095 & 1 \\
+ attention + curriculum + energy + R\&F & 0.753 & 0.128 & 1 \\
+ intrinsic + curriculum + energy + R\&F & 0.834 & 0.068 & 1 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\par\vspace{2.5pt}{\scriptsize\itshape The anchor value is the zero-shot evaluation of the nominal-trained
learner on the small-battery regime (0.7646).  A configuration that closes
the $-0.064$ gap to the rule (0.8290) is a publishable algorithmic result.
The innovations are reported on one seed each; the curriculum+energy run
on three seeds (0.831, 0.830, 0.831) confirms the single-seed reading.}
\end{table}

\emph{Innovation 1 + 2 + 4 (curriculum + energy shaping + R\&F).}
Curriculum over battery stress lifts the small-battery evaluation from
$0.765$ to $0.831$ (three seeds: $0.831$, $0.830$, $0.831$), essentially
tying the rule ($0.829$).  The gain is $+0.066$ and is the largest single
improvement found; it is the only innovation that closes the energy gap to
within noise.

\emph{Innovation 6 (graph attention).}
Attention makes the small-battery result \emph{worse} ($0.753$ vs $0.831$).
The MLP actor is better than the attention actor on this task at this
budget; the attention's permutation invariance buys nothing the ego-centric
observation does not already provide.

\emph{Innovation 7 (intrinsic motivation).}
Count-based intrinsic motivation has no effect ($0.834$ vs $0.831$,
$+0.003$).  The exploration bonus does not change the policy because the
coverage reward already provides a dense enough signal.

\emph{Innovation 5 (difference credit).}
Difference credit is a small positive on the nominal configuration
($0.959$ vs $0.952$, $+0.007$, not resolved) but \emph{hurts} on
small-battery ($0.816$ vs $0.831$, $-0.015$).  Per-agent marginal credit
interferes with the team-level energy management the curriculum teaches.

\emph{Innovation 3, 8, 9, 10 (shuffling, action repeat, adversarial,
feasibility-aware planning).}  Shuffling is a no-op for a shared policy and
needs an observation rework; action repeat and adversarial layouts are
implemented but not yet evaluated; feasibility-aware planning is designed.

\emph{Combination.}  The best single innovation on small-battery is the
curriculum ($+0.066$, ties the rule).  Combining it with difference credit
makes the result \emph{worse} ($0.816$), and adding attention makes it
worse still ($0.753$).  The innovations do not compose; each one that
touches the reward or the observation interferes with the ego-centric
summary that is the actual driver of performance.  The residual on energy
regimes is therefore a genuine limitation of the method class at this
budget, not a knob that has not been turned.

\emph{The paper's thesis.}  The corrected learner beats the strongest rule
on 4 of 6 regimes (nominal, low connectivity, failure, multi-failure) and
ties or loses on 2 (small battery, spread start).  The certification
framework is what makes the split visible: a single ``does learning beat
the rule'' number would have hidden it, and the same framework is what
caught the three defects (sign-flipped entropy, 25 gradient steps,
train-CK evaluation) that made the original number wrong.

% This replaces the boxed superseded section once the corrected evidence exists.

\section{Results}
\label{sec:results}

All numbers in this section are produced by the protocol of
Section~\ref{sec:protocol}: a controller is frozen before it is measured, and
every controller is measured on the same \tokRuleScenes{} held-out scenes
(seeds from \texttt{1000}), none of which a training run saw.  The rules and
the random control are deterministic given a scene, so their spread over the
table is scene-to-scene; each learned row is one frozen policy per training
seed, so the spread of a learned row is seed-to-seed.  The ceiling is the
teleporting placement oracle, which reaches $1.000$: the configuration is
coverable, so every shortfall below is a controller shortfall and not an
infeasible instance.

\subsection{The corrected comparison}
\label{sec:results_corrected}

Table~\ref{tab:remeasured} is the whole of the comparison.  Three readings are
worth spelling out.

\emph{First, the rules reproduce.}  The pre-correction table of this report
was measured on scenes $0$--$4$; re-run at the current code on the same
scenes, the four rule rows reproduce it to three decimal places ($0.372$,
$0.784$, $0.953$, $0.972$).  The measuring apparatus therefore did not change
between the two versions of the report, and a number that moved is a number
the learner moved.

\emph{Second, the learner now clears every rule.}  MAPPO with the corrected
implementation and the new observation (Section~\ref{sec:results_abl}) reaches
\tokEgoShapeCK{} over \tokEgoShapeN{} training seeds, against
\tokRuleReactiveLocalCK{} for the strongest hand-written rule (the
unprivileged local-assignment reactive rule).  The difference, learner minus
rule, is \tokLearnerMinusRule{} of persistent coverage with a 95\% interval
of \tokLearnerMinusRuleCi, and \tokGapVerdict.  The gap of $0.298$ that an
earlier version of this report reported is retracted in
Section~\ref{sec:history}: it was a property of a learner whose entropy bonus
was sign-flipped and whose update ran 25 gradient steps per run, and of a
protocol that compared a policy in training against a rule at rest.

\emph{Third, the deployment policy is the sampled one.}  The argmax policy
(the deterministic reading of the same network) reaches \tokEgoShapeDetCK{}:
the gap between the two rows is the cost of the exploration the deployed
policy keeps, and it is small.

\subsection{What closes the gap: the observation, not the bug fixes}
\label{sec:results_abl}

Two interventions were applied to the corrected learner together, so their
contributions are separated by an ablation:

\begin{itemize}
  \item \emph{Bug fixes only} (the corrected PPO implementation, the old
        observation): \tokBugFixCK{} (95\% interval \tokBugFixCi,
        \tokBugFixN{} seeds).  This is the number the report's earlier
        ``fixed learner'' would have produced under the corrected protocol.
  \item \emph{+ ego-centric observation and distance shaping} (bearings to
        the three nearest under-covered sensors; potential-based shaping):
        \tokEgoShapeCK.  The increment is $\approx 0.093$ of persistent
        coverage, and the two intervals do not overlap: the change to the

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Stress regimes and generalisation}
\label{sec:results_stress}

The learner is trained on the nominal configuration only, then rolled out

the zero-shot generalisation measurement: a controller that holds the two
invariants on the training distribution but fails on a regime the certificate
declares feasible has failed as a controller, not because the instance was
infeasible.

Zero-shot, the learner is ahead of the best rule on 4 of 6 same-architecture regimes, and the mean difference across them is +0.019.


\emph{The certificate separates the regimes the learner can be held to
account on from the ones it cannot.}  The stress table has a structural
feature that is the point of the paper: on the regimes whose architecture
has the same observation and state sizes (battery, connectivity, failure,
deployment), the frozen policy is evaluated as-is; on the regimes that
change the architecture (\texttt{single\_pad} changes the size of the
centralised state), no policy trained on the nominal architecture can even
be loaded, and the table says so instead of pretending.  A zero-shot
measurement is only defined where the input space is the same, and a table
that reports NA there is reporting a property of the architecture, not of
the controller.



The qualitative pattern is what the framework is for.  The learner is ahead
of the strongest rule where the task is about \emph{where to be} (nominal,
low connectivity): the reactive rule is a greedy local policy, and a policy
that has 200 episodes to learn the scene statistics beats a hand-written
greedy rule that has none.  The learner loses where the task is about
\emph{what to conserve} (small battery): the rule's recharge logic is
explicit, and the learner, which never saw a depleted battery during
training, has no behaviour for it.  A reader told only that ``the learned
controller beats the rule'' or only that ``it loses'' would be told a
half-truth; the certificate is what separates the two statements into the
regimes where each is true.

\subsection{Network certificate}
\label{sec:results_network}

The network is not the binding constraint at 80 m scale: an OMNeT++/INET
co-simulation certifies PDR $\approx 0.998$ with a range margin of $22\times$
over the mission scale (Section~\ref{sec:radio}, artefact
Simulation/omnet_uav2/).  The binding constraints are coverage geometry and
energy; the certificate makes the ideal-observation assumption of the RL
simulator a measured statement rather than an assumption.

\subsection{History of this measurement}
\label{sec:history}

The first version of this report reported a gap of $0.298$ (learner $0.674$
vs the reactive rule $0.972$) and attributed it, through controlled arms, to
the learner's observation and credit rules.  Three defects were later found
in the implementation and in the protocol; each is described in
Section~\ref{sec:second_sprint}.  The old measurements are retained in the
repository as a record under \texttt{docs/}, and are not part of the evidence
base of this version.

\section{Results}
\label{sec:results}

All numbers in this section are produced by the protocol of
Section~\ref{sec:protocol}: a controller is frozen before it is measured, and
every controller is measured on the same \tokRuleScenes{} held-out scenes
(seeds from \texttt{1000}), none of which a training run saw.  The rules and
the random control are deterministic given a scene, so their spread over the
table is scene-to-scene; each learned row is one frozen policy per training
seed, so the spread of a learned row is seed-to-seed.  The ceiling is the
teleporting placement oracle, which reaches $1.000$: the configuration is
coverable, so every shortfall below is a controller shortfall and not an
infeasible instance.

\subsection{The corrected comparison}
\label{sec:results_corrected}

Table~\ref{tab:remeasured} is the whole of the comparison.  Three readings are
worth spelling out.

\emph{First, the rules reproduce.}  The pre-correction table of this report
was measured on scenes $0$--$4$; re-run at the current code on the same
scenes, the four rule rows reproduce it to three decimal places ($0.372$,
$0.784$, $0.953$, $0.972$).  The measuring apparatus therefore did not change
between the two versions of the report, and a number that moved is a number
the learner moved.

\emph{Second, the learner now clears every rule.}  MAPPO with the corrected
implementation and the new observation (Section~\ref{sec:results_abl}) reaches
\tokEgoShapeCK{} over \tokEgoShapeN{} training seeds, against
\tokRuleReactiveLocalCK{} for the strongest hand-written rule (the
unprivileged local-assignment reactive rule).  The difference, learner minus
rule, is \tokLearnerMinusRule{} of persistent coverage with a 95\% interval
of \tokLearnerMinusRuleCi, and \tokGapVerdict.  The gap of $0.298$ that an
earlier version of this report reported is retracted in
Section~\ref{sec:history}: it was a property of a learner whose entropy bonus
was sign-flipped and whose update ran 25 gradient steps per run, and of a
protocol that compared a policy in training against a rule at rest.

\emph{Third, the deployment policy is the sampled one.}  The argmax policy
(the deterministic reading of the same network) reaches \tokEgoShapeDetCK{}:
the gap between the two rows is the cost of the exploration the deployed
policy keeps, and it is small.

\subsection{What closes the gap: the observation, not the bug fixes}
\label{sec:results_abl}

Two interventions were applied to the corrected learner together, so their
contributions are separated by an ablation:

\begin{itemize}
  \item \emph{Bug fixes only} (the corrected PPO implementation, the old
        observation): \tokBugFixCK{} (95\% interval \tokBugFixCi,
        \tokBugFixN{} seeds).  This is the number the report's earlier
        ``fixed learner'' would have produced under the corrected protocol.
  \item \emph{+ ego-centric observation and distance shaping} (bearings to
        the three nearest under-covered sensors; potential-based shaping):
        \tokEgoShapeCK.  The increment is $\approx 0.093$ of persistent
        coverage, and the two intervals do not overlap: the change to the
        observation, not the bug fixes, is what closes the gap.
\end{itemize}

Persistent and Fault-Tolerant UAV-IoT Coverage: A
Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework
for Joint Coverage, Connectivity, and Energy
Management
Himanshu Nagwanshi
Surya Prakash S
Harsh Varshney
Gaddam Viswaijeth
CS24BT055@iitdh.ac.in
CS23BT068@iitdh.ac.in
cs23bt004@iitdh.ac.in
CS23BT076@iitdh.ac.in
Department of Computer Science and Engineering
Indian Institute of Technology Dharwad, Dharwad, India
Abstract—UAV swarms can provide temporary wireless cover-
age for Internet-of-Things (IoT) deployments in areas where fixed
infrastructure is unavailable, damaged, or insufficient. Persistent
operation is considerably harder than one-shot deployment be-
cause coverage, inter-UAV connectivity, battery depletion, limited
charging resources, and UAV failures are tightly coupled. This
paper formulates the problem of maintaining at least K UAVs
over every ground sensor while preserving a connected swarm
and respecting finite energy and safety constraints. The resulting
decision process is modelled as a cooperative Decentralized Par-
tially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP). We
propose a Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO)
controller under centralized training and decentralized execution
(CTDE). Each UAV executes a shared policy from local observa-
tions, while a centralized critic is used only during training. The
learned controller is combined with an explicit feasibility mask,
a reserve-UAV recovery mechanism, and a small infrastructure-
side charging arbitration procedure. A focused survey of ten
closely related studies shows that coverage, connectivity, energy-
aware operation, recharge scheduling, and fault recovery have
largely been studied separately or in different combinations.
The proposed framework targets their intersection and defines
an evaluation protocol covering persistent coverage, connectivity
availability, recovery delay, energy consumption, charging con-
tention, safety, and scalability. Numerical performance claims
are intentionally deferred until the proposed experiments are
completed.
Index Terms—UAV-IoT networks, persistent coverage, fault
tolerance, multi-agent reinforcement learning, MAPPO, Dec-
POMDP, connectivity maintenance, energy-aware coordination.
I. INTRODUCTION
The Internet of Things (IoT) increasingly operates in envi-
ronments such as agricultural fields, disaster-affected regions,
industrial sites, and remote monitoring areas where fixed
communication infrastructure may be sparse or temporar-
ily unavailable. UAVs can provide rapidly deployable aerial
communication or sensing support because their positions
can be changed in response to the spatial distribution of
demand. Energy-efficient UAV control has therefore been stud-
ied for communication coverage, fairness, and connectivity,
while aerial-base-station placement has been formulated as a
learning-based spatial optimization problem [1], [2].
The practical difficulty changes substantially when the
network must remain operational for a long mission rather
than only achieve good coverage at one instant. The sup-
plied project model considers N UAVs operating over M
ground sensors, finite batteries, communication links between
neighboring UAVs, a limited number of charging pads, and
the possibility that an active UAV fails during the mission.
The central requirement is persistent redundancy: every sensor
should remain within coverage range of at least K active
UAVs. At the same time, the UAV communication graph
should remain connected so that information can be forwarded
through the swarm to a ground station or data sink.
These requirements conflict. A UAV that moves toward an
uncovered sensor may leave a coverage gap elsewhere. A
UAV that returns to charge may be the only communication
bridge between two groups of UAVs. A failure removes
both its coverage contribution and its communication links,
requiring the remaining swarm to reconfigure. Charging is
also a shared resource: several UAVs can become energy-
critical simultaneously while only a small number of pads are
available. Persistent service therefore requires a joint decision
process rather than a sequence of unrelated coverage and
charging heuristics.
A centralized controller faces a rapidly growing joint action
space. In the proposed discrete action model, each UAV selects
one of six actions: hover, move in one of four cardinal
directions, or charge. The joint action space consequently
contains 6N combinations. This growth does not by itself
make centralized learning impossible for every small swarm,
but it makes explicit joint-action enumeration and centralized
policy design progressively less attractive as N increases. A
decentralized execution architecture is therefore desirable for
scalability and fault containment.
Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) provides a
natural framework for this setting. CTDE allows a central-
ized critic to use information unavailable to the individual
UAV during training while retaining decentralized policies
during deployment. MAPPO is particularly suitable because
it combines centralized value estimation during training with


=== PAGE 2 ===
a policy-gradient actor that can be executed independently by
each agent.
The research question addressed in this work is: Can a
decentralized MAPPO policy maintain persistent K-coverage
and swarm connectivity while coordinating finite battery us-
age, charging, and single-UAV failure recovery without requir-
ing a centralized trajectory controller?
The contributions are:
1) A unified system model coupling persistent K-coverage,
inter-UAV connectivity, finite battery energy, charging
contention, and UAV failure recovery.
2) A CTDE MAPPO framework with parameter-shared
decentralized actors, a centralized training critic, hard
action feasibility masks, and an explicit reserve-UAV
recovery mechanism.
3) A focused literature synthesis showing the differ-
ence between existing coverage, connectivity, recharge-
scheduling, and fault-tolerant approaches and the com-
bined problem considered here.
4) A benchmark and metric protocol designed to sepa-
rate coverage, connectivity, energy, recovery, safety, and
scalability effects rather than relying only on a single
aggregate reward.
The remainder of the paper is organized as follows. Section
II presents the literature survey and research gap. Section
III defines the system architecture and mathematical model.
Section IV presents the proposed MAPPO algorithm. Section
V specifies the comparison models. Section VI defines the
performance metrics and evaluation protocol. Section VII
concludes the paper.
II. LITERATURE SURVEY
The survey is restricted to work that is directly related to
at least one of four components of the target problem: UAV
coverage/control, inter-agent connectivity, persistent energy-
aware operation, or fault-tolerant swarm recovery. The ten
core papers in Table I are discussed comparatively rather
than as isolated summaries. MAPPO is cited separately as the
underlying learning method [3].
A further recent line of work integrates communication and
control directly within MARL. MAPPO itself is adopted from
Yu et al. [3]. Sun et al. formulate joint resource allocation and
3D trajectory control and use action masking for constrained
hybrid actions [11]. Carvalho and Aguiar address decen-
tralized multi-agent coverage path planning with parameter
sharing, CTDE, safety filtering, and zero-shot generalization
[13]. Zhuang Chen et al. formulate UAV trajectory design
for emergency communication as a constrained MDP and
explicitly account for energy and turning behavior [12]. These
works reinforce the practicality of CTDE, action masking, and
structured rewards, but their primary objectives differ from
persistent redundant coverage with explicit failure recovery.
A. Research Gap
The literature can be grouped into complementary but
incomplete directions. Energy-efficient coverage works jointly

not integrate persistent sensor coverage and energy-aware

combinations of health state, outage memory, target assign-
ment, or coverage objectives [9], [14].
Based on this surveyed set, we did not identify a sin-
gle framework that simultaneously models: (i) persistent K-
coverage of fixed IoT sensors, (ii) explicit swarm-connectivity
preservation using communication-graph criticality, (iii) finite
battery operation with contested charging pads, (iv) failure-
triggered reserve-UAV recovery, and (v) decentralized exe-
cution of the motion policy. The proposed formulation is
designed around this intersection. This is a survey-derived gap
statement, not a claim that no related component has ever
appeared in the broader literature.
III. SYSTEM MODEL
A. System Architecture
The system contains N active UAVs, one reserve UAV,
M fixed IoT sensors, a ground data sink/base station, and
S charging pads distributed within the operating region Ω.
UAVs provide sensor coverage through a range-limited air-
to-ground link and form a multi-hop communication network
among themselves. Sensor data reaches the sink through the
UAV communication graph whenever the graph is connected.
For tractability, the UAVs fly at a common nominal altitude
z0, so the decision process operates in the horizontal plane
while the altitude remains part of the physical state. Let

J. Safety Constraints
The environment enforces
∥vi(t)∥≤vmax,
pi(t) ∈Ω,
∥pi(t) −pj(t)∥≥dsafe, ∀i̸ = j.
(19)
An action is masked if it violates a locally predictable hard
constraint such as workspace bounds, speed, minimum sepa-
ration, or invalid charging. Connectivity is not assumed to be
perfectly predictable from one-hop observations; instead, the
actor receives the local bridge-risk feature ρi and the team
reward explicitly penalizes connectivity fragility. This avoids
claiming a global connectivity guarantee from purely local
information.
K. Failure and Recovery
A failure event changes Fi from 0 to 1 at the detection
instant tf. One reserve UAV is maintained with sufficient
energy for deployment when feasible. After a detected failure,
the reserve is activated and the active UAVs continue using
their decentralized policies. The recovery time is defined as
τf = inf {τ ≥0 : nd(tf + τ) ≥K, ∀d} ,
(20)
when recovery is achieved before the evaluation horizon. If
recovery is impossible under the available fleet, the event is
reported as an unrecovered failure rather than assigning an
artificial recovery time.
A recovery-time guarantee is therefore conditional: the
reserve mechanism can reduce the time required for reconfig-
uration, but it cannot mathematically guarantee restoration for
arbitrary sensor layouts, fleet sizes, or multiple simultaneous
failures. This distinction is important for a realistic system
model.

Since the learner maximises expected return while the control
objective of (22) is a minimisation, the team reward of (23)
is the negated weighted cost, and the two are equivalent up
to sign. Table IV defines each term and gives the initial
weights used in this work. The weight λO is chosen to
dominate the secondary efficiency terms, so that the learned
controller does not sacrifice persistent service merely to reduce
energy consumption or flight distance. The individual objective
components remain separate evaluation metrics rather than
being hidden inside a single final score.
All six quantities are dimensionless and lie in [0, 1], so the
weights are directly comparable; Ut and Critt are already
normalized in (10) and (13). The values are initial settings
to be tuned on a validation set; the ordering λO ≫λD ≥
λR > λC ≥λE ≥λW is the part on which the formulation
depends.

The control interval is chosen so that the relative displace-
ment between two consecutive steps, 2vmax∆t = 2 m, is
smaller than the safety distance dsafe = 5 m; a coarser step
would allow a closing pair to cross the separation constraint
between two samples. The charge increment is quoted per step
and is therefore scaled with ∆t. The resulting charge time
is shorter than a real constant-current pack of this capacity
would require, because a real pack would not complete a full
charge within a tractable episode; this is stated as a modelling
assumption rather than a physical prediction, and it means
the cost of charging contention in (IX) is a lower bound.
The nominal altitude is consistent with the coverage radius: a
74◦downward sensor at 50 m yields a footprint half-width
of 37 m. The two power entries are distinct: Pelec is the
total avionics and communications budget, whereas Ptx is the
radiated transmit power, which is bounded by the 1 W ceiling
of IEEE 802.11 and is two orders of magnitude below the
avionics budget.
Within scope are spatial K-coverage, range-limited UAV
connectivity, battery depletion, charging contention, single-
UAV failure recovery, collision avoidance, and decentralized
motion-policy execution. The primary model intentionally
abstracts stochastic PHY-layer fading, detailed aerodynamic
dynamics, obstacles, wind, battery aging, GPS denial, sensor
failures, and multiple simultaneous UAV failures. These can
be introduced as subsequent stress-test layers after the base
control problem is validated.
IV. PROPOSED ML ALGORITHM
A. CTDE MAPPO
The proposed algorithm uses parameter-shared MAPPO.
During training, the centralized critic observes st while every
actor uses oi(t). During deployment, the critic is removed and
each UAV evaluates the same shared policy:
ai(t) ∼πθ (ai | oi(t)) .

B. Action Feasibility Mask
Before the sampled action is executed, the simulator eval-
uates the predicted next position and applies the following
checks: workspace bounds, maximum speed, minimum UAV
separation, charge validity, and connectivity-preservation con-
straints. If a candidate movement would disconnect the com-
munication graph, it is masked in normal operation. During
an active recovery event, the connectivity rule remains a hard
constraint unless the simulator enters a predefined recovery
mode in which temporary reconnection is required by the
recovery objective.
This separation between policy learning and hard feasibility
is important. The neural network learns how to trade off
several feasible actions, while the safety layer prevents the
network from selecting actions that violate non-negotiable
physical constraints.
C. Failure-Aware Execution
When a failure event is detected, the environment removes
the failed UAV from the active graph, activates the reserve
UAV if the reserve is available, and updates the local obser-
vations. The reserve UAV uses the same shared actor after
insertion into the mission. The other UAVs also re-evaluate
their local bridge-risk and coverage information. No prediction
of the failure event is required; the controller reacts to the
observed state change.
D. Mapping from Model to Algorithm
The algorithm is deliberately aligned with the system model.
Sensor positions produce the coverage quantities in (7)–(10);
neighboring UAV positions produce the communication graph
in (11); battery and action information produce the energy
state in (14); charging requests enter the assignment problem
in (18); and failure indicators activate the recovery process
in (20). Thus, every actor input corresponds to an explicitly
defined state quantity and every learned action has a defined
environmental effect.
E. Training and Generalization Protocol
Training episodes should randomize sensor layouts, initial
UAV positions, initial battery levels, charging-pad locations
within the allowed region, and failure times. A simple curricu-
lum can be used: first train under no failures, then introduce
single failures, and finally introduce simultaneous charging
contention and near-disconnection scenarios. The final model
should be evaluated on held-out random seeds and scenario
configurations not used for parameter tuning.
A practical implementation can use a multilayer perceptron
for the shared actor and centralized critic with normalized
numerical features and masked action logits. If fixed-length
neighbor features are insufficient, a permutation-invariant
pooling operation or a small attention encoder can be added
without changing the underlying Dec-POMDP formulation.
A recurrent policy should be introduced only if experiments
show that instantaneous observations do not provide sufficient
temporal information.

G. Implementation Plan
The implementation follows the three-stage validation strat-
egy presented in the project plan. The objective is to validate
the swarm-control logic before introducing detailed wireless-
channel complexity.

V. COMPARISON MODELS
The comparison design preserves the practical baselines
from the project presentation and adds recent learning-based
methods required for a meaningful research comparison. The
practical baselines test whether any adaptive coordination is
useful; the MARL baselines test whether the proposed CTDE
MAPPO design provides advantages over other learning for-
mulations.
The fixed, greedy, and reactive controllers correspond di-
rectly to the practical alternatives already identified in the
project plan. MAD-DDQN provides a value-based MARL

Service con-
tinuity
Fraction of mission time for which both the K-coverage and
connectivity requirements are satisfied. Measures end-to-end
persistent service.
Outage
severity
Time-integrated under-coverage during degraded and recovery
intervals. Measures how much service is lost, not only whether a
recovery eventually occurs.
Reserve
uti-
lization
Number of reserve activations, activation delay, and reserve mission
time. Measures whether replacement capacity is used effectively.
Recovery
Mean/95th-percentile τf , recovery success rate, and
unrecovered-failure count. Measures fault tolerance directly.
Energy
Total energy consumption, energy per successfully covered
sensor-slot, minimum battery level, and threshold violations.
Measures efficiency and safety margin.
Charging
Mean wait time, denied requests, number of concurrent requests, and
pad utilization. Captures contention and scheduling quality.
Movement
Total distance flown and unnecessary-movement ratio Wt. Quantifies
motion overhead.
Safety
Collision events, out-of-bounds events, and hard-constraint violations.
These should ideally be zero.
Scalability
Policy inference time and metric degradation as N and M increase.
Tests the reason for adopting decentralized execution.
Stability
Mean and standard deviation across independent random seeds;
training convergence time/episodes. Measures reproducibility.
uses explicit action masking. Vanilla MAPPO is an internal
ablation rather than a literature method: it applies the same
learner to the unmodified task so that the effect of the
proposed system design can be separated from the effect of
the learning algorithm. Because these literature methods solve
related but not identical tasks, any adaptation to the common
simulator must be documented rather than presented as an
exact reproduction.
All models use the same sensor layouts, initial UAV posi-
tions, battery conditions, charging pads, failure traces, episode
durations, and physical safety constraints. Where a literature
method requires a different input representation or native ac-
tion space, the adaptation should preserve its decision structure
as far as possible. Results should be reported on common
metrics when an exact one-to-one mapping is not available.
Ablation experiments should additionally remove one
proposed mechanism at a time: connectivity-criticality in-
put/reward, reserve-UAV recovery, charging arbitration, and
action masking. This distinguishes improvements caused by
the MAPPO learning method from improvements caused by
the proposed system design.
VI. PERFORMANCE METRICS
The evaluation should report separate metrics for service
quality, connectivity, energy, charging, recovery, movement,
safety, and scalability.

A. Evaluation Scenarios
The first experiment varies sensor density while keeping the
fleet fixed. The second varies fleet size to examine scalability.
The third varies battery capacity and charge rate. The fourth
varies the number of charging pads. The fifth varies Rcomm
and Rcov to create well-connected, marginally connected, and
difficult coverage geometries. The sixth injects single-UAV
failures at early, middle, and late mission times and at both
central and peripheral locations.
For each scenario, the same random seeds and initial con-
ditions must be used for all comparison models. At least five
independent seeds are recommended for each configuration,
with the mean and sample standard deviation reported. When
space permits, confidence intervals should also be shown. Raw
reward curves may be included as supplementary evidence, but
the principal conclusions should be based on the task-specific
metrics in Table IX.
Ablation experiments should separately remove: (i) the
connectivity-criticality feature/reward term, (ii) the reserve-
UAV mechanism, (iii) charging arbitration, and (iv) action
masking. This identifies whether each proposed component
contributes a measurable effect. In particular, the comparison
between the full proposed framework and vanilla MAPPO is
necessary to distinguish improvements caused by MAPPO it-
self from improvements caused by the domain-specific system
design.
VII. EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN MATRIX
The final evaluation should vary the dominant environmen-
tal factors independently before combining them. Table X
maps each experiment to a specific research question.
VIII. CONCLUSION
This paper defines a persistent and fault-tolerant UAV-IoT
coverage problem in which the swarm must jointly man-
age redundant sensor coverage, inter-UAV connectivity, finite
battery energy, charging contention, and UAV failures. The
proposed solution uses MAPPO under centralized training


=== PAGE 10 ===
and decentralized execution, complemented by explicit fea-
sibility masking, infrastructure-side charging arbitration, and
a reserve-UAV recovery mechanism.
The formulation is intentionally implementable. The learned
actors operate on quantities that a physical UAV can measure
or estimate locally, while the simulator computes the corre-
sponding global quantities for training and evaluation. The
literature survey indicates that the required components exist
individually across coverage, connectivity, recharge schedul-
ing, and fault-tolerant MARL studies, but the combined
problem formulation remains a meaningful integration target.
The experimental phase should therefore focus on whether
the proposed combination produces measurable improvements
in persistent coverage and recovery while keeping energy,
charging, movement, and safety costs under control.
No performance advantage is claimed in this report before
the experiments are executed. Once the implementation is
complete, the same metric and comparison structure can be
used to report both absolute results and trade-offs, including
the possible cost of more conservative movement in exchange
for improved connectivity robustness or faster recovery.

Persistent and Fault-Tolerant UAV-IoT Coverage: A
Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework
for Joint Coverage, Connectivity, and Energy
Management
Himanshu Nagwanshi
Surya Prakash S
Harsh Varshney
Gaddam Viswaijeth
CS24BT055@iitdh.ac.in
CS23BT068@iitdh.ac.in
cs23bt004@iitdh.ac.in

Department of Computer Science and Engineering
Indian Institute of Technology Dharwad, Dharwad, India
Abstract—UAV swarms can provide temporary wireless cover-
age for Internet-of-Things deployments where fixed infrastruc-
ture is unavailable, damaged or insufficient, but persistent opera-
tion couples coverage, inter-UAV connectivity, battery depletion,
charging contention and UAV failures. This paper formulates
the problem of maintaining at least K UAVs over every ground
sensor while preserving a connected swarm, and models it as a
cooperative Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision
Process (Dec-POMDP). We argue that the evaluation method-
ology is the unsolved part of this problem: a coverage ratio
reported without an achievability reference cannot distinguish
a strong controller from an infeasible configuration, and the
widely used service-continuity metric is identically zero for every
policy on any instance whose sensor set admits no trajectory
that keeps it K-covered while the swarm stays connected. We
therefore introduce a feasibility-certified evaluation framework
that derives a rigorous lower bound on the fleet size needed for
K-coverage of a bounded region, supplies a teleporting placement
oracle that certifies the instance is coverable — at the reported
configuration the ceiling is 1.000, so it normalises to the identity
and its only information is that the instance is coverable at all
— and replaces the degenerate joint-constraint metric with non-
degenerate time-averaged and refresh-time metrics. Applied to
the project report’s own configuration, the bound shows that
configuration to be provably infeasible for the region requirement
and for a measured minority of random sensor layouts, and the
conventional area-surplus criterion certifies nothing.
On the corrected configuration the framework is paired with a
centralized-training decentralized-execution MAPPO controller
with parameter-shared actors, a hard connectivity feasibility
mask, a reserve-UAV recovery mechanism, charging arbitration
and PHY-derived links. A hand-designed reactive rule outper-
forms the learned controller by 0.298 of persistent coverage (95%
interval [0.248, 0.349]). Figure 1 is the argument of this paper
in one picture. Controlled arms bound how much of the gap
each alternative explanation can account for, and every arm’s
upper confidence limit lies below the gap of 0.298 — by margins
that are small but positive, the smallest of them 0.161 — so
none of the explanations the arms test can be the whole of it The
residual is consistent with the credit assignment of a shared team
reward, and the cheapest test of that diagnosis does not resolve
it: the per-agent local critic’s difference is -0.035 of persistent
coverage (95% interval [-0.079, +0.009]), which includes zero The
residual is also consistent with causes that the arms do not test
— the possibility that the rule was tuned against the evaluation
scenes, the limit of a decentralised policy class — and we do
not claim to have excluded them. The paper’s physical-model,
feasibility, protocol and determinism claims are recomputed by
an automated claim audit (38 items, 0 failing), which does not
audit the results of Section VIII, and every number that comes
from a measurement is generated from the artefact it is measured
in, and the path-loss expression of the physical-layer model is
shown to be algebraically the one an independent standards-
faithful simulator evaluates — a constant 0.012 dB offset at every
distance and exponent tested — with a transmit-power negative
control that shows why only the algebraic equivalence is claimed.
Index Terms—UAV-IoT networks, persistent coverage, fault
tolerance, multi-agent reinforcement learning, MAPPO, Dec-
POMDP, connectivity maintenance, feasibility bounds, evaluation
methodology.
I. INTRODUCTION
The Internet of Things (IoT) increasingly operates in envi-
ronments such as agricultural fields, disaster-affected regions,
industrial sites, and remote monitoring areas where fixed
communication infrastructure may be sparse or temporar-
ily unavailable. UAVs can provide rapidly deployable aerial
communication or sensing support because their positions
can be changed in response to the spatial distribution of
demand. Energy-efficient UAV control has therefore been stud-
ied for communication coverage, fairness, and connectivity,
while aerial-base-station placement has been formulated as a
learning-based spatial optimization problem [1], [2].
The practical difficulty changes substantially when the
network must remain operational for a long mission rather
than only achieve good coverage at one instant. The sup-
plied project model considers N UAVs operating over M
ground sensors, finite batteries, communication links between
neighboring UAVs, a limited number of charging pads, and
the possibility that an active UAV fails during the mission.
The central requirement is persistent redundancy: every sensor
should remain within coverage range of at least K active
UAVs. At the same time, the UAV communication graph
should remain connected so that information can be forwarded
through the swarm to a ground station or data sink.

rule still reaches 0.648 persistent coverage on that instance, while the service-continuity metric is identically 0.000 for every policy. (b) On the corrected,
